# Stellar Discovery Trust Layer

## Build application · SCF #46 · Open Track

**TokenJunkieLabs requests USD 38,000 equivalent in XLM for 400 prospective delivery hours over 150 days from actual award acceptance.** The work installs a useful paid Stellar service with two independently operated merchants, two independent buyer operators and the same selected operation through two independently operated facilitators.

The product is open-source, self-hostable merchant and buyer tooling. It carries an approved API request, dataset or paid MCP tool through native settlement, complete useful output, fulfillment and operating handover. The merchant controls its source and terms. The buyer controls its keys, request and spending. Another engineer can reopen the installation and recover unfinished work.

The working development baseline comprises **18 distinct team-operated purchases totaling 411,000 stroops, or 0.0411 native testnet XLM**, with network fees recorded separately. The funded milestones establish independent customer operation, repeated use and production receiving from that baseline.

## 1. Customer problem and commercial model

An API or data-service operator needs to expose a useful resource to agent applications while retaining access rules, source meaning and commercial control. A buyer needs the complete result it approved and a way to resolve an interrupted paid request. The difficult join spans four records: approved request, settled transfer, delivered output and accepted fulfillment or accounting.

Current x402 reports show the practical need for that join. One October 2 report described payment-bearing requests rejected because a merchant required POST while the reference client retried GET; health and catalogue checks had appeared normal. The author subsequently corrected the server. An October 3 report described settlement without a discovery listing; a separate operator later reported successful indexing of its own resources and explained the facilitator diagnostics in that thread. These were Base deployments. They show how a healthy catalogue or settled payment can leave the customer's task unfinished. Our Stellar implementation retains the exact request and each original outcome so the unfinished step can be recovered. [Method report](https://github.com/x402-foundation/x402/issues/3657) · [Discovery report](https://github.com/x402-foundation/x402/issues/3677)

We serve recurring API/data-service operators, the developers using their results and agencies commissioned to integrate them. A fixed-fee implementation delivers one agreed operation and a handover the receiving engineer can maintain. Further care has its own scope. The commissioning payer, merchant controlling the resource and independent buyer may be different organizations. The workorder names each role, its source and host authority, payment responsibility and acceptance owner. The merchant retains its API or product receipts; TokenJunkieLabs invoices the implementation.

The selected customer task and the priced unit are recorded together. A complete report may require several paid pages. A handover may contain many files or transport chunks. The buyer retains per-request and aggregate spending controls while the operating record shows whether the whole task is complete. A later reporting period, changed source edition, fresh query or new order gives the same buyer a reason to use the service again.

## 2. Product architecture and control

Six connected components form the application: the merchant's private source/release workspace; its HTTP or MCP operation; the native Stellar SDK and configured facilitator; the buyer's private approval and spending state; complete result and delivery records; and merchant fulfillment/accounting. Merchant and buyer services run on their operators' hosts. Approved operations are public; administration, provider credentials, signer references and operating state stay private.

| Stage | Implemented customer control |
| --- | --- |
| Review and publish | Review a source edition or named live query, its arguments and schema, public fields, output limits and complete payment alternatives. Save rights, route, network, asset, recipient, atomic amount and authorization lifetime. Changes or withdrawal become new reviewed states. |
| Connect the source | Preserve original types, missing/null values, pagination and snapshot/live meaning. Customer-controlled credential or OAuth aliases select access and the existing quota/cache state. Retain the edition behind each result. |
| Approve and purchase | Save the actual endpoint, method or tool, arguments, payment option and result scope. Match remote schema and challenge to that selection before signing. Keep the per-payment ceiling and the application's aggregate reservation/budget owner. |
| Settle and deliver | Use the configured native SDK/facilitator for verification and settlement. Save the server's response, full output, byte identity and durable merchant notification. Independently reconcile transaction network, asset, payer, payee and atomic amount. |
| Use and maintain | Receive every selected page or file into the customer's existing application, query, report or workbook. Preserve the parent acquisition and earlier source editions. Existing order and finance authorities control fulfillment, refunds and accounting. |
| Deploy and receive | Select the release, HTTPS service, restricted administration and supervision. Drain, restart, roll back and restore with the original configuration, history and complete customer files. |

The native x402 flow reuses the existing Exact Stellar scheme, token contracts and facilitator supported/verification/settlement interfaces. For paid MCP, the HTTP endpoint, tool and arguments remain distinct from the payment resource. An unsigned call obtains the challenge; the full payment option must match the saved quote before the signed call is dispatched. The official MCP SDK transports the payment and settlement metadata.

Server confirmation, independently observed transfer, complete useful output, receiver acknowledgment and order fulfillment remain separately visible. An uncertain signed reply retains its dispatch state for reconciliation. Reopening a consumed quote returns saved work. Recovery of a complete retained result uses that saved result. A new request or changed purchase gets its own review. Complete export and restore carry the configuration, history and referenced files; the receiving host supplies current authorized secret references.

Browser, CLI, MCP and installed Applications use these same saved workspaces. Native source registrations connect setup, operation and lifecycle while preserving each source adapter's data semantics. The existing request-collection, buyer-to-Operations and document-analysis extensions retain their own original recovery operations; their pending native receiving stages are reported separately from the completed examples below.

## 3. Why Stellar and the ecosystem fit

Stellar settles the approved operation. Buyer approval binds the complete request to its network, asset, recipient and integer atomic amount. Existing libraries and payment services sign, verify and settle; our application connects the transfer to complete output and practical merchant fulfillment.

| Existing component | What it supplies | What this product contributes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Native Stellar x402 and OpenZeppelin facilitator | Supported payment options, buyer-authorization verification and settlement | The approved HTTP/MCP request, original source, complete output and recoverable receiving operation |
| Vellar discovery | Optional discovery extension and best-effort catalogue updates independent of settlement | Saved offer/schema/terms and a complete source edition that remains usable through customer review and handover |
| Stellar MPP | Charge for individual requests; Session with funded channels and cumulative commitments | An existing Charge workbench that retains the native challenge, request and merchant profile through concurrent preparation and restart |

OpenZeppelin, Vellar, Veridex and Periplo remain payment-infrastructure choices. Rumble Fish is developing facilitator, discovery and SDK capabilities. We build on those components and return reusable integration and receiving improvements to the public source.

A retained comparison found 27 Vellar offers and two Periplo offers with no shared seller/route identity. The funded two-facilitator deployment therefore includes registering and integrating the same useful operation with both. Each completion will retain the selected provider's actual scheme, network, asset and fee policy. This makes the cost and effort of changing payment infrastructure observable while the merchant service and buyer task remain defined.

[Stellar x402 documentation](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/build/agentic-payments/x402) · [Stellar MPP documentation](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/build/agentic-payments/mpp)

Each installation starts from one complete workorder: recurring task and commissioning payer; merchant, buyer and receiving operators; source rights and access; selected host/runtime; exact request, full output and priced unit; approved network, asset and terms; repeat-use trigger and acceptance owner. ## 6. Customer selection and repeat use

Four human conversations inform the current decisions. Veridex invited an open testnet design partnership after declining an external testing budget; the subsequent proposal is USD 1,500 over five business days. Nansen first referred the read-only Holdings integration internally, then declined pursuing it on October 12 at 16:15:57 UTC. Its historical proposal remains USD 2,400 over five business days. CoCart's founder asked about introductions, the commissioning payer, referral compensation, responsibilities and contracting; its proposal is USD 7,200, 60 planned hours and fifteen business days. Blockscout expressed interest on October 12 and reported no current integration budget; the proposed workshare is USD 4,800 over ten business days.

Bryce owns the continuing favorable relationships and subsequent agreements; the Nansen decision remains in the original case history. The first CoCart customer remains to be selected. Source-platform participation and the organization commissioning an installation are recorded separately. These responses are customer learning and proposed work, with acceptance and collected revenue retaining their actual stages.

Selection favors a recurring buyer task, permitted source, accountable merchant host, independent receiving application and agreed payer. The buyer engineer connects the operation to the application's existing authorization, signer, aggregate budget and destination. The receiving engineer uses the full output, records corrections and reopens the same operation. The maintainer completes a source or terms change, recovery or receiving task during handover.

Eight October 12 data-platform proposals apply this method to AceMQ, OpsTree, Cazton, Natron, Severalnines, Altinity, Percona and ScaleGrid. Their separately retained scopes total USD 52,500 for 350 planned hours, priced at USD 150/hour. At the common USD 95/hour labor assumption, modeled labor is USD 33,250 and the remainder before other costs is USD 19,250. A 25% labor overrun leaves USD 10,937.50 before other costs. These are proposed economics; they do not select the funded customers or establish revenue. Scope, original customer ownership and actual effort determine the next implementation estimate.

The six funded packages retain their own hours. Qualified commercial work is scheduled and costed separately so the same adaptation is assigned once. No combination of overlapping offer cohorts is presented as booked business.

## Recurring economic-report installation

The maintained economic application supports recurring analyst briefings and complete county reports in one saved project. Staff retain original source editions, review the selected reporting period and calculation profile, produce the useful report, publish its original files through the existing merchant, and receive the paid result through the original Buyer. Release watches and series vintage histories drive later analyst acquisitions; county profiles retain their selected geography, industries, reporting quarter and price basis. A second engineer can receive the complete economic project, reopen its saved plans and reports, and continue the same reporting procedure.

**Useful customer task and roles.** An economic research desk, reporting team or software application needs a defined report for a later period while retaining the basis of its previous publication. The commissioning workorder names the organization paying for implementation, the merchant controlling the source and publication, the independent buyer using the result, and the maintainer accepting the operating handover. It selects the source rights and access, series or county/industry coverage, calculation choices, reporting interval, required output, native payment terms and receiving application. The independent operator assesses the finished task by opening the whole delivered report and tracing its measures to retained current and baseline observations or original county source rows.

**The paid unit.** A published analyst edition offers its complete offline `briefing.html` with local measures, source views and CSV/JSON exports, or the corresponding `briefing.json`. A published county edition offers one complete `report-package.json.gz`: the selected report, every original predecessor edition, complete manifests, original HTML/PDF/JSON/CSV, methodology and predecessor comparisons. The customer can receive that package in its own directory, reopen any included edition and download the original files. Current county report files are also available individually. Each advertised resource identifies its exact byte count, SHA-256 and content type. The buyer prepares that GET and reviews the original network, asset, recipient, integer atomic amount and authorization lifetime. The original Stellar SDK, facilitator and Buyer perform verification, settlement, retained output and recovery. Each selected resource keeps its original request and price; the installation workorder specifies the agreed complete output and aggregate spend.

**Acquire the right source edition.** A saved release watch names the series or original briefing template, observation interval, baseline date and whether to catch up every applicable vintage or select the latest available one. The operator retains the complete official response pages and reviews calendar changes, series vintage dates, coverage and source meaning before saving the plan. Calendar dates describe the publisher’s release schedule; the returned series vintage dates drive actual observation acquisitions. An incomplete source interval exposes the exact additional selection to acquire. The operator then selects a planned date, and the original FRED observation provider acquires its exact series, period and as-of selection into the same economic project.

**Board-to-FRED migration and current-publication reporting.** The same economic project retains the original Federal Reserve Board package, official series crosswalk, complete source catalogue and saved migration. The analyst reviews the selected source series, frequencies, periods and mapped FRED series before running the complete current-publication programme. Its Current publications desk acquires all mapped publications for that saved plan or attaches an already completed programme. A retained request, progress and original output let the operator continue the same job after a closed browser or restarted host.

The analyst opens each original series and its full comparison rows, with exact decimal strings, source scales, period labels, missing codes and original-file locations. The six result categories distinguish equal values, changed values, unavailable values on both sides, changed availability, Board-only periods and FRED-only periods. Retrieval timestamps describe the current public tables; the original API release/vintage workflow retains its separate as-of selection. A later collection creates another retained edition while the earlier report remains available.

**Complete publication delivery and independent receiving.** The selected edition carries its original programme inputs, full source manifest and transports, all comparison rows, HTML report, native project and complete downloadable archive. Large originals stream to the receiver; the browser pages the original row file without replacing the complete result with a sample. The receiving engineer opens the delivered native project, attaches the retained programme and continues from the same saved migration and source population. The [installed receiving guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/355e98f3ea45ccc322d2a6a8651e522f14ab3bec/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/fred/ddp/PUBLISHED-WORKSPACE.md) covers the browser, CLI, typed client and HTTP/MCP operation.

**County source and report production.** A saved profile selects the reporting geography, industry comparisons, original reporting quarter and price basis. The operator imports the complete retained BLS QCEW intake and original CPI capture into the same project, produces the full report and retains its source availability and disclosure/missing-value meaning. Later editions keep their original predecessor, report files and complete comparison. The merchant publishes the saved report package, so the customer receives the same useful files reviewed by the operator.

**A recurring edition.** The template retains the original series/comparison selection, relative-change choices, precision and meaning. Its calendar policy names the number of complete months, the selected-series observation-date rule and any trailing months to omit. Missing markers retain their original dates; a quarterly observation date remains its source period label. Preview exposes every selected series’ source and window coverage, changed units/frequency/seasonal adjustment, new or departing periods, and changes to current values and baselines. Saving a successor retains the normal analyst review and complete report, ready for the original publication and customer path. The full predecessor comparison is also available as HTML, CSV and JSON.

Reopening a saved report or resuming its download retains the original purchase. A later reporting window or newly retained source edition begins the next useful operation: review the selected acquisition, inspect the changed report and approve its publication. Catch-up completion belongs to the selected watch and exact release snapshot, so a later snapshot can reveal an additional series revision on a date already processed. Previous plans and buyer reports remain readable with their original source and values. Source retrieval time, API real-time/vintage dates and observation-period labels retain their distinct meanings.

County customer receiving saves its original destination with the same purchase before writing report files. If the browser or host restarts, the customer reopens that native intent and continues the same receiving directory. A separately downloaded complete package can be received on another host through the installed command. Publishing or transferring an existing county edition reuses its original compressed package bytes.

## Coastal model-input installation

A coastal engineering team needs the selected station records in the format its model and analysts actually use, with the original observation, units, time basis, datum, quality fields and later corrections still traceable. Moffatt & Nichol’s published [numerical-modeling practice](https://www.moffattnichol.com/solution/numerical-modeling) and [Digital services](https://www.moffattnichol.com/digital) provide a concrete prospect for this installation. The original workshare proposes USD 18,000 for 150 planned hours over six active working weeks: one selected study, up to five NOAA stations and five years, one agreed CSV/JSON model-input convention and one deployment environment. The original inquiry was sent on October 12, 2026 to Moffatt & Nichol’s published general-routing mailbox, requesting the coastal, Digital or small-business outreach colleague. The firm would choose the actual study and acceptance reviewer and would retain calibration, engineering interpretation and client recommendations.

The merged Coastal Source Operations product carries the source work from a saved station and historical window through original response capture, reviewed source editions, selected input mappings, a complete study release and a returned-file decision. It preserves observation and prediction products separately, exposes complete coverage and source receipts, and retains the original station-specific datum and time meaning. A saved release fixes its source editions, selected windows, mapping and review. Later working-study edits do not change the files already supplied to the analyst.

The installation workorder names four operational responsibilities. The commissioning organization agrees and pays for its engineering scope. The merchant’s source operator controls the selected capture, review and release, including the rights and terms attached to the original data. An independent buyer uses the advertised result in its own analysis. The receiving engineer owns the installed configuration, restoration and support handover. One person may perform several staff tasks where the agreement permits it; the funded independent-merchant and independent-buyer targets retain their stated separation.

The quote identifies that resource, its selected edition, price, native payment requirements and expected complete result. Source archives, other formats and query pages retain their own advertised access and request terms. The USD 18,000 implementation proposal is separate from those resource purchases. A later observation period or an explicitly reviewed source correction supplies a reason to acquire another useful edition. Retrying the same request or reopening an already acquired edition preserves that original operation.

The engineering sequence begins with the client’s actual station selection and input specification. Staff retain the originals, inspect the selected periods and quality fields, and map source columns to the receiving model’s declared headings, units and missing-value rules. The reviewer decides whether the complete selected input is suitable for release. The analyst can then obtain the released files through the existing application or standard-library Python client, verify every selected file and original-source archive, continue an eligible native dataset query across all its cursors, and reopen the retained files offline. A selected query dataset follows the existing 250,000-row and 256 MiB parser limits; complete released study files remain the source for a larger handoff. A returned input is kept as its own original version. Full comparison and an explicit receiving decision preserve changes and ambiguous rows for the assigned engineer.

## 7. Threat response and useful-outcome measurement

T2 includes the actual deployment's threat assessment, monitoring thresholds, notification destinations, accountable responders and material remediation.

| Failure to operate | Control and observation |
| --- | --- |
| Changed source, request or terms | Match exact source generation, request and approved payment alternative before dispatch. Retain rejection cause, quote age, source expiry and capacity refusal. |
| Uncertain payment or incomplete delivery | Reconcile the original intent and transfer, retain partial output/entitlement state and recover unfinished work. Measure outstanding age and time to useful output. |
| Unauthorized access or exposed private state | Validate issuer, audience, subject, scopes, expiry and current authority. Restrict administration and protect credentials, keys, claim tokens, private bodies and backups; retain access/rotation observations. |
| Observation or notification failure | Keep the last useful capture, incident and original notification attempts. Retry the same event; measure coverage, alert, acknowledgment and recovery time. |
| Restart or state loss | Restore the selected backup and reconcile later operations. Reopen the same support case and full output on the receiving host; measure time, retained history and active effort. |

Count each independent organization or person once across agents and wallets. The funded payment counts remain ten completed purchases in total across the two buyers in the T2 window and thirty in total in the T3 window. Each purchase joins its distinct approved payment intent, native transfer and complete purchased output. Transactions are deduplicated within their network; amounts, refunds and fees retain their own asset and atomic units.

Report the associated customer tasks separately using their original acquisition, job or application-run identity. A paginated acquisition retains its parent and all child page intents. The Queens HPD example therefore contains two 10,000-stroop purchases and one complete 144-row task. Its 100-row and 44-row pages remain available inside the same receiving edition. Report every started parent alongside its completed result and required fulfillment.

A later call using that order records another application outcome and its units. A new native payment records another purchase. Reopening a saved response, resuming a download or recovering the same execution retains the original identities.

These units are already present in the product. The dataset session carries its `sessionId`, page `intentId`, completed-page and acquired-row state. The prepaid application retains `orderRef`, `requestId`, `requestSha256` and `units` against the original reservation. Cohort reporting joins those records with actual native settlement and receiving outcomes. Returning use identifies the fresh period, changed edition or distinct customer request.

For each customer, record the previous method and, where available, the active effort and corrections of a prior execution. ## Federal awards: complete funding research, workshares and receiving

The [Federal awards and workshares product](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/f374ab2ec216324ab00147810f7972acf8523353/products/federal-awards/README.md) now includes complete funding-report authoring, publication, merchant delivery and editable customer receiving. The full product is merged in the maintained Merchant Workspace through [PR177](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/pull/177) and [PR330](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/pull/330), with the report edition at source revision `f374ab2ec216324ab00147810f7972acf8523353`. It joins the original USAspending award and transaction workspace, research dossier, SF30 merchant, SF88 buyer, native merchant tools and managed Applications. The [complete funding-report guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/f374ab2ec216324ab00147810f7972acf8523353/products/federal-awards/FUNDING_REPORTS.md) provides the implemented operator and customer workflow.

**Customer task and commercial roles.** A contractor, research service or agency commissions a recurring review of the federal awards relevant to its defined work. The commissioning payer funds that installation; the merchant operates the agreed data or research service; the buyer approves and acquires a particular useful edition; the receiving analyst uses the whole result; and a second engineer maintains the installation. The original workorder names those parties, their source rights, the award population and reporting period, the public output, the receiving application, the priced unit, acceptance and update frequency. Private fit assessments, relationship notes and commercial terms stay within the selected working handover.

The useful paid unit is the complete dataset or research report agreed in that workorder. The implemented report delivery carries its public explanation, exact transaction history, original award editions, every source page and both observations used in a comparison. The merchant prepares that entire retained file through the original SF30 asset service. SF88 buyer review binds the original request, complete file size and digest, network, asset, recipient and atomic amount. The installation charges for the agreed curated service and delivery; every edition identifies the underlying official award source. T1 applies this existing product to the selected customer’s source population, publication terms, merchant host and receiving application.

**Operate the complete research job.**

1. **Select and retain the original award source.** Save the actual agency, date, award-type and industry filters or receive the complete existing source collection. Preserve the request and all returned pages, select the immutable award edition, and inspect the prime, parent award, awarding agency and funding agency. Source observation time remains separate from the agency’s action and performance dates.
2. **Capture the award’s funding history.** Continue the official transaction endpoint through its terminal page. Accepted pages and their normalized occurrences commit together. Review the chronological modifications and fiscal-year totals with exact decimal values, negative and zero changes, missing fields, repeated IDs and conflicting occurrences. A stopped request resumes its original capture and continuation.
3. **Prepare the whole workshare.** Save the fit, explanation of funding changes, proposed implementation, complete deliverables, acceptance, owner, case link and next action. The completed capture’s source fingerprint and the review revision bind that assessment to the original records. Put the research question, sources, findings and citations in the existing dossier when that is part of the customer job.
4. **Prepare and review the complete report.** Select the completed capture and, when relevant, an earlier complete observation of the same award. Enter the public title, publisher, purpose, findings, implications and use terms. The draft binds the current saved assessment revision and complete source fingerprint. Review the readable chronology, fiscal-year totals, repeated and conflicting occurrences, changed fields and original observation times. Publish that exact reviewed report digest. The public editor’s text enters the report; the private assessment remains in the research workspace.
5. **Publish the selected merchant operation.** Prepare the original SF30 asset bundle with the report’s fixed public route, origin and actual payment terms. Its original catalog carries the complete file, digest and payment choices. The native seller service exposes that immutable report edition through the configured facilitator and the merchant’s normal HTTPS deployment. Changes to report content or route and terms retain their own reviewed edition and preparation history.
6. **Receive the whole useful output.** The buyer uses the original SF88 review, signing and response-file workflow. The receiving application adopts that completed inbox intent, verifies the exact original response file and retains its payment and source provenance. It opens the complete report and extracts readable HTML, editable JSON, transaction CSV and every original source response and receipt. A directly supplied complete report file enters the same receiving workspace. The customer can prepare a revised public explanation while retaining the received source report and its original acquisition.
7. **Continue the installation.** Restore the whole workspace on the receiving host or receive the original award and transaction capture into an existing workspace. Reopen the saved application, continue the assessment, compare a later source observation and retain earlier delivered editions. Restored report merchants rebuild their original bundle and catalog inside the receiving workspace from its retained report bytes and selected terms. The receiving engineer continues the original job, intent, file export and workspace identities through interruption and restart.

## Environmental provider intake: complete source editions, commissioning and receiving

The recurring customer task is to bring a provider's observations into an existing environmental-data intake process, review the source's meaning and deliver a complete handoff that another engineer can use. The provider may correct a station definition, change a variable mapping or supply a new observation period; the receiving team needs the resulting edition and the earlier accepted one. Axiom's [published intake process](https://www.axiomdatascience.com/best-practices/SubmitDataSensors.html) makes that need specific: it prefers ERDDAP access, documents variable-name inconsistencies that require manual intervention, and requests scientific and technical context alongside the data.

### Commercial scope and accountable roles

The original Axiom workshare was sent on **12 October 2026 at 11:22:14 UTC**, with a complete workshare, fillable intake worksheet, acceptance cases and operating guide. It proposes **$12,600 for 96 engineering hours over 18 active business days**: three representative provider feeds, one client-managed Linux installation and one agreed file/command receiving integration. Proposed payments are **$6,300 at kickoff and $6,300 after receiving acceptance**. Eight of the 96 hours cover in-scope implementation corrections during the first 30 days after acceptance. The delivery clock starts with the selected source access and receiving environment available. This is a sent proposal; an accepted engagement, issued invoice, payment and customer installation have not been recorded.

|Role|Decision and responsibility in the proposed installation|
|  ---  |  ---  |
|Commissioning payer and acceptance owner|The final workorder names the contracting payer, the three selected feeds, the receiving environment and the person accepting the delivered integration. The proposal names Axiom's intake team as the receiving organization; agreement is still to be reached.|
|Source provider and scientific contact|Supply authorized access, source licensing and attribution, station and time context, processing history and existing quality definitions. The designated scientific team owns interpretation, calibration and any newly requested quality evaluation.|
|TJLabs implementation engineer|Configure and integrate the existing application, resolve implementation defects, deliver the complete permitted source and operator materials, and carry out the agreed receiving walkthrough and included support.|
|Merchant and independent buyer for a funded deployment|Separately agree the authorized published operation, complete result, price unit, payment asset and terms, recurring buyer task and buyer application. These are deployment-selection decisions under the common grant plan.|
|Receiving engineer and later maintainer|Operate the agreed file/command boundary, inspect the full received source and review, reopen the installation, correct a later edition and retain the earlier accepted output.|


The workshare allocates 16 hours to source/receiving design, 28 to provider configuration, 24 to installation and handoff integration, 20 to receiving and operator handover, and eight to initial support. These are the case's fixed-fee delivery allocations. They do not change the application's $38,000 / 400-hour / 150-day budget. A favorable human reply goes to Bryce before another external send; the original company case remains the commercial record.

### The complete useful operation

1. **Select and retain the source.** The operator chooses the actual grid or station-table query and retains the original metadata, query, data responses and acquisition record. The agreed station set, observation period, variables, units, source authority and permitted use define the population. The included historical examples provide reusable public reference inputs; customer commissioning uses the separately selected authorized feeds.
2. **Review the source and provider context.** The operator inspects every selected field and station, keeps the original values and quality flags, and records explicit column, time and edition decisions. Dataset CSV policy and provider data-edition choice are separate controls. Missing scientific context stays visible in a working review until the responsible person resolves it.
3. **Save and produce the complete edition.** The application records an immutable reviewed revision and its source, mapping and evaluator version. The full handoff carries the original capture, names-and-units observations, station definitions, variable mappings, time and quality disclosures, a missing-value sidecar and the reviewed profile. A completed-intake export follows the actual review's readiness result.
4. **Receive the actual output.** The receiving installation validates the complete bundle, retains its source and review, provides the same exact ZIP for later download and reopens the saved result. The commissioned file/command integration places that handoff in the customer's agreed environment and reports the actual receiving outcome.
5. **Correct and return.** A changed mapping, provider context or observation period becomes a separately reviewed edition. Lost save responses, concurrent reviews and later exports remain tied to their original requests and history. The receiving engineer can compare the new edition while preserving earlier accepted files and meaning.

For a funded paid installation, the workorder would define the priced unit as a complete agreed source/data edition or bounded useful query. If that task needs several priced requests or pages, the buyer sees the aggregate cost and receives all of the accepted result. A new period, revised source edition or a new authorized analytical request can create a later useful purchase. Redownloading, transferring or recovering the same output continues its original purchase. The merchant's source rights, actual Stellar terms and original financial record remain explicit; a local dataset or review export is engineering evidence rather than a new network purchase.

### Working product and demonstrated receiving

The [complete ERDDAP product](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/public-commons-sprint-2026/tree/184abaf54ce864973f7a28fc8fb835b83497ef5b/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/erddap) supports source acquisition and inspection, immutable native dataset editions and queries, provider profiles and saved reviews, full source/customer exports, original merchant and buyer integration, typed clients, 36 MCP tools and the operator UI. The maintained standalone selection is **erddap-provider**. Its [operating guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/5f7143f88bb28fbd0c1b63a913545633c475afd6/products/erddap-provider/OPERATING.md) carries the original selected build and runtime-install procedure; Managed Applications exposes **Ocean and environmental data** for the same initialized workspace.

The current selected source explicitly includes five retained NOAA capture ZIPs: three 27-row MUR grid selections, the 144-row NDBC station selection and a 432-row longer NDBC period. The station selections overlap and retain separate source identities. Their complete metadata, DDS, DAS, JSON, CSV and acquisition records are listed in the [source index](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/5f7143f88bb28fbd0c1b63a913545633c475afd6/products/erddap-provider/SOURCE.json).

The same operation saved three provider-review revisions. It exercised exact-save recovery, concurrent-head rejection, review export and independent bundle receiving. The selected canonical-JSON profile retains its actual unresolved scientific-contact appointment; its current review is useful and its ready-export status remains false.

An actual comparator upgrade also exposed and resolved a continuity problem: unchanged source/profile records could produce a different comparison report after a software upgrade. New review identities now bind the evaluator version; historical receiving deterministically reproduces the supported original evaluator. The continuation reproduced both original review ZIPs byte for byte, preserved their saved head and history through retries and reopened their independent receiving. It accepted the supported historical lexical and Decimal representations and rejected an unknown evaluator and a changed report with a recomputed hash.

The public and standalone source merges are complete. The original selected package build, installed receiving and full browser continuation are still pending with their existing operation. The demonstrated native results establish the source/review/receiving behavior; customer commissioning and the funded independent-use milestones remain to be completed.

## Datasette editions and customer analysis

A customer who works from a published Datasette table needs the entire selected edition, its source meaning and an editable analysis that another operator can receive. The source operator reviews the table or query, complete capture, source columns, explicit projection and business key, then prepares the original dataset publication. The customer application opens that same reviewed edition or its retained original page bundle in the maintained Analysis workspace. The merged source operator, publisher and customer Applications share the installed Datasette selection, so a receiving engineer can install and reopen the complete workflow from one maintained source revision.

The complete WRI geothermal example contains 189 records and 26 returned positions (25 physical columns plus the row locator) across 22 countries, with 12,563.55 MW of disclosed capacity. All four response pages, ordered schema, publisher attribution and CC Attribution 4.0 metadata accompany the source. The reports keep capture time separate from the observations' historical years: 110 records have no stated capacity-data year. Exact numeric spellings, blank or null observations and original business identifiers remain available alongside country, owner, fuel, capacity-year, generation-year and source-quality summaries.

The customer application provides the original source rows, saved SQL, published HTML/JSON/table reports, an Excel workbook and a full editable workspace transfer. A receiver can reopen the same analysis, save a country selection, produce a fresh delivery and transfer that edited workspace onward. Its Applications integration, browser, native command and typed client use the same retained workspace and original Python installation. The source desk also retains upload progress and the original receiving request across browser reload and connection loss. The operator can inspect the saved outcome and continue the same request; whole-workspace delivery carries the original source, editions, selections and publication state. The complete publisher and installed-browser programmes continue this same source through runtime installation, managed application startup, original upload and selection-response interruption, whole-workspace receiving, and desktop/mobile reopening. Continuations retain the reviewed source commit, original application operation and earlier browser history.

For a commissioned service, the workorder names the source/release operator, commissioning payer, independent buyer and receiving engineer; defines the complete table or query edition and useful analysis output; records the reviewed source/license and paid-resource terms; and names the later data release that justifies repeat use. Source adaptation and publication, buyer integration, deployment, customer operation and independent handover use the existing six funded packages. The current 400-hour / $38,000 / 150-day grant plan supplies the shared commissioning scope.

The receiving engineer opens the complete editable directory and referral package, including earlier editions and the decisions used to select the destination. The [operating guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/10e017744344ce831bd78fc1ea4c2e3143172d29/products/human-services-directory/OPERATING.md) gives the native, browser, connected and installed workflow.

**Delivered source and current operation.** Merchant [PR402](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/pull/402) and public [PR2444](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/public-commons-sprint-2026/pull/2444) / [PR2456](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/public-commons-sprint-2026/pull/2456) contain the complete source engine, mapping and referral domain, industrial operator, typed SDK, Merchant tools, Applications contribution and installation selection. The retained publisher basis contains 85 original Open Referral HSDS 3.3.1 files and 20 original HL7 Human Services Directory STU1 files. HSD's published mapping targets HSDS 2.0.1 and FHIR 4.0.1; the product exposes the 3.x migration decisions for review. The completed source operation imported all 24 original CSV tables plus nested JSON, indexed 65 rows and retained 86 relationship observations, including ambiguous and unresolved candidates. An edited service description produced one changed record and 23 unchanged records against the original CSV edition. Its FHIR source leg retained the complete 39-resource published eLTSS Bundle, including 98 resolved and two unresolved references. The [source notice](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/10e017744344ce831bd78fc1ea4c2e3143172d29/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/fhir_directory/SOURCE_NOTICE.md) preserves attribution, and the [complete receiving programme](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/10e017744344ce831bd78fc1ea4c2e3143172d29/products/human-services-directory/RECEIVING.md) continues through selection, the original referral, handoff, browser, connected operation and installed receiving.

**The useful Stellar service.** A commissioned merchant can offer one authorised directory edition, one complete reviewed service-selection result, or an agreed refresh and change report. Its workorder fixes the source edition, complete output, priced unit, receiving application and event that makes a later purchase useful. A new published edition, changed service availability or a distinct customer query can supply that later task. The buyer approves the selected asset, amount and request through the existing merchant/buyer flow. The native facilitator delegates verification and settlement to the official Stellar x402 SDK; the acquired result then enters the directory application with its original source and selection. The application retains full directory and referral data in the selected operator workspace. The network transaction pays for the agreed service. The [native merchant and facilitator](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/10e017744344ce831bd78fc1ea4c2e3143172d29/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/native-facilitator/README.md) provide the payment implementation, while the existing application payment register supplies the actual purchase history.

**Commissioning within the funded programme.** This is a source-specific implementation option inside the existing two-merchant/two-buyer, $38,000 / 400-hour / 150-day plan. The completed reusable product is the starting point. T1's existing 80-hour resource integration and 40-hour authority/handover packages connect the selected publisher, actual service output and independent receiving operator to that customer's application. T2's existing 70-hour provider deployment and 50-hour response packages operate the same paid result through both facilitators and recover interrupted payment/delivery cases. T3's existing 90-hour mainnet rollout and 70-hour recovery/handover packages carry recurring useful purchases, the original service history and a complete receiving-host restoration. The programme's existing cohort targets apply across the selected installations. The commissioned workorder assigns each actual adaptation once, with source access, deployment charges, staff participation and customer acceptance attached to its original owner.

The independently usable result is a selected service and referral that the next operator can understand, update and continue. Source refresh, mapping correction, changed availability and receiving-host restoration use the retained application history. The [product source and entry points](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/10e017744344ce831bd78fc1ea4c2e3143172d29/products/human-services-directory/README.md) and the original SCF delivery give the complete maintained installation.

## Recurring subscription delivery and streaming-data commissioning

A data team operating RisingWave can commission a complete customer-delivery service around an existing table or materialized view. The useful task is a reviewed operational report, changed-record feed or typed dataset that another application actually consumes. The initial installation selects up to two subscriptions and two complete outputs in one customer environment. A later reporting period, corrected source edition or distinct customer query provides the reason for another purchase.

**Customer and commissioning roles.** The workorder names the commissioning payer, source owner, merchant operator, independent buyer and receiving engineer. The source owner approves the actual relations, publishable fields, keys, retention window and customer rights. The merchant controls publication and payment terms. The buyer selects the useful output and its receiving application; the receiving engineer takes over the installed service and retained customer work. A RisingWave delivery partner can introduce and manage the customer relationship while TokenJunkieLabs supplies the agreed source, payment, application and handover engineering. These responsibilities follow the original proposed customer workshare.

**Why this source needs an operating product.** RisingWave subscriptions expose an initial snapshot and later insert, update and delete records. Resuming from a saved timestamp is inclusive, and changes older than the configured retention period cease to be available. The delivered source therefore keeps the original capture, exact typed values, progress and change order together. It preserves the paired records of an update, presents added, removed and changed rows for review, and gives a retention-gap rebuild its own explicit decision. A customer can receive a complete reviewed edition while earlier delivered editions remain usable. [RisingWave subscription contract](https://docs.risingwave.com/serve/subscription).

**Implemented foundation and current receiving.** The complete source is merged in [public product PR2306](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/public-commons-sprint-2026/pull/2306) at df13417fc1b96949a333a10b0790fb0312627d5d and in [Merchant Workspace PR266](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/pull/266) at 61698bfd10411413decae5c334b41a2c28d4d5a9. Its 40-file native product provides source and subscription review, retained snapshots and changes, keyed edition comparisons, reviewed publication, recurring receiving and complete customer transfer. Browser, CLI, merchant MCP and managed Applications compose the same source, publisher and buyer workspaces. The [operating guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/public-commons-sprint-2026/blob/5fed7c1d79ef7e5a841fd7a5d11f0d3d337a8dd5/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/risingwave/README.md) preserves the original installation and native entry points.

The current integration step is complete native-to-installed receiving in the original RisingWave operation. That operation selects RisingWave 3.1.0 and the retained 1,342-record NYC HPD source, then carries initial and corrected editions, interruption recovery, publication, original buyer receiving and cold Applications reopening through the same saved case. Its source, customer work and operating result stay joined as the installation advances.

**Commercial scope and economics.** The original offer was sent to RisingWave’s first-party sales address on October 12, 2026 at 12:58:58 UTC. It proposes **USD 10,000 for 80 planned hours over fifteen active working days within five weeks**, with USD 3,000 / 4,000 / 3,000 written-acceptance milestones. The complete scope covers one environment, up to two existing relations/subscriptions and two typed outputs, initial and corrected editions, interruption recovery, retention rebuild and one recurring receiving workflow. The partner retains its customer relationship and publication decision. Original sent-offer record; complete nine-file commercial and receiving package.

At the application’s USD 95/hour planning assumption, the offer represents USD 7,600 of planned labor and **USD 2,400 before other costs**. A 25% effort overrun produces 100 hours, USD 9,500 of modeled labor and **USD 500 before other costs**. Its effective offered rate is USD 125 per planned hour. If the first USD 3,000 installment is received at commencement, it funds 31.58 modeled labor hours; the case must align the next accepted delivery and actual collection with the remaining work. Actual accepted terms, effort, invoices and receipts belong to that existing commercial workorder.

**Stellar value and the existing funded work.** The selected paid operation is the complete reviewed dataset, report or query result required by the buyer’s task. Its saved approval binds the selected source edition, route, request and exact network/asset/recipient/amount. The existing x402 Stellar integration carries the buyer’s signed authorization through verification and settlement; the original buyer receives the complete output and can reopen acquired work. Source data and private credentials stay in their source and customer workspaces. A changed edition receives its own review and terms. [Stellar’s x402 integration](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/build/agentic-payments/x402).

If this installation is selected for the funded cohort, its remaining engineering belongs to the application’s existing six packages:

* **T1, days 1–30:** implement the customer’s actual source/runtime, publishable projection, typed consumer, route, terms and buyer setup; then have a second operator reopen the installation and perform the agreed source or terms change. The receiver opens both the earlier acquired edition and the reviewed current result.
* **T2, days 31–90:** register the same useful service with both independently operated facilitators and carry the original customer operation through the existing ten-purchase/seven-day testnet target. Deploy its threat assessment and monitoring, then recover an interrupted settled request and a delivery failure while retaining the original payment and full useful output.
* **T3, days 91–150:** commission the production hosts and recurring mainnet task within the existing thirty-purchase/fourteen-day target, including both buyers returning on another day. Complete off-host retention, credential rotation, receiving-host restore, later-operation reconciliation and the independent maintainer’s support case.

The original two-merchant/two-buyer programme remains **400 prospective hours / USD 38,000 over 150 days from actual award acceptance**. The workorder assigns each customer adaptation once to its funded package or separately commissioned scope. Source publication already completed before the award supplies the starting product.

**Customer learning to carry into following installations.** At commissioning, the same case will record the chosen useful output, baseline time to produce and receive it, time to usable corrected output, actual source changes that prompted repeat use, operator recovery time, installation effort and support demand. Its purchase history keeps approved intent, settled asset amount, provider, complete output and customer acknowledgment together. These observations establish whether the service saves work for the buyer, whether it can be operated by a second engineer, and which adaptations can be reused in the next commissioned installation.

## Source monitoring: useful editions and complete reviewer handover

OpenSanctions's [monitoring guide](https://www.opensanctions.org/docs/monitoring/) identifies a concrete integration task: retain a counterparty portfolio and earlier decisions, receive later data editions, reconcile changing identifiers, and route the relevant changes to the customer’s reviewer. Its original model separates identity resolution from the relevance of a designation to that customer. The [licensing choices](https://www.opensanctions.org/licensing/) distinguish hosted API use, internal bulk screening and redistribution. The customer workorder selects the applicable source and service rights alongside the actual receiving interface.

### Working product and completed receiving

The maintained source-monitoring application composes the original NDJSON and native dataset engine. It retains complete FollowTheMoney editions, statement inputs when supplied, original delta operations, source and row lineage, canonical identifiers and referents, portfolio editions, native request records, and case decisions with their previous history. Publisher content changes and observation-metadata changes remain separately visible. A reviewer can follow the selected source and update through the same case, record a reasoned decision, and export the entire operated workspace.

The October 12 source evaluation received the original September 30 and October 12 UN editions, containing 2,926 and 2,923 records respectively, together with the three original nonempty delta files dated October 1, 6 and 11. Its two-row source-inspection portfolio and original case continued through the new client and installed CLI. The 46-step native operation received the original files again, used the original dataset query engine, reviewed the selected source change, retained all three case events, and exported the complete working state. Closing and reopening the same application returned the same saved state. A separate receiving workspace imported the full customer export and returned the same complete case history and usable native query. All three native listeners closed successfully.

The [complete typed client, installed selection and operating guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/0abb1f4cb324646d3652a3a9f066a586837cc4c2/products/source-monitoring/OPERATING.md) are merged in [PR239](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/pull/239). ## Groundwater scenario modelling and receiving

## Service recovery that reaches the buyer’s books

### The customer outcome

A buyer needs the useful service it purchased and a correct record of what happened when delivery failed. The merchant may recover the output, agree a partial return or identify a remaining correction. The buyer then needs the credit to reach the right expense item, reporting period and accountant handoff. Keeping those links saves staff from repeatedly matching support tickets, payment records, exported files and bookkeeping rows.

The Service-to-buyer operation carries that work through one saved customer case. The merchant selects its Service report and explicit monetary basis. Its configured accounting operator reviews the adjustment and the returned-transfer evidence. The buyer receives the complete capture, codes the original purchase and credit, resolves period issues and issues the period. The accountant’s reviewed return comes back to those original rows. A receiving engineer can reopen the continued project with its source, decisions and customer files.

### Architecture and operator control

The existing merchant workspace owns the Service terms, report, proposal, prepared intent and native outcome. The configured accounting workspace verifies the selected payment and adjustment and exports the original purchase, linked credit and complete adjustment statuses. Buyer Expenses owns source intake, exact native-unit allocations, issue dispositions and issued periods. The Accountant workspace owns its handoff and permitted returned fields.

Each step uses the configured owner’s existing workspace and request journal. Before dispatch, the operator reviews the exact input and original workspace selection. When a response is interrupted, recovery reuses the retained request and body; an already committed result is returned before applying a current-version check. Appending the outcome preserves other operators’ intervening case work. The complete export carries the applications, buyer state, issued period, accountant files and original requests together.

The monetary decision stays explicit: the Service report supplies the observed event and reviewed basis; the responsible operator authorizes the adjustment. The original purchase, adjustment status, returned-transfer proof and buyer coding remain separately inspectable throughout receiving.

### Current implementation and example

The complete implementation is merged in public [PR2236](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/public-commons-sprint-2026/pull/2236) at [628b9c1bba2438ca36015bed6e08acb414a9f4ce](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/public-commons-sprint-2026/tree/628b9c1bba2438ca36015bed6e08acb414a9f4ce), integrating the 24-file product: browser, case API, CLI, MCP, operating guides and native entry with original-job recovery. Its complete installed Merchant Workspace adoption is merged in [PR200](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/pull/200) at [6bb02489fbb3360e609b7450a4378244eb9b07a9](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/tree/6bb02489fbb3360e609b7450a4378244eb9b07a9), with all 35 files covering the product, existing owner dependencies, managed source selection, operators and guides. The original owner has also published the complete 962-file native source closure for the combined receiving operation. That operation’s completed result is still pending. The separately preserved evaluator package retains its checked source edition and actual source-only validation.

The selected demonstration input is the retained Woo order 18 DEVELOPMENT/testnet case: a purchase of 2,500,000 atomic units and a partial return of 1,000,000 in the same original asset. It preserves the payment, event, adjustment, effective date and return proof, labeled CHAIN_TRANSFER_MATCHED_RPC_TESTNET. This is controlled native RPC source; it supplies no new public-ledger observation, independent customer purchase or fiat valuation. The completed combined result will establish the actual buyer rows, issued period and accountant-return identities.

## Merchant settlement, customer billing and accountant receiving

A working Stellar merchant needs the useful paid result and a financial record its customer and accountant can continue. The maintained product joins native settlement accounting, customer invoicing, dated receipt allocation, credit notes, installment schedules and Xero document receiving around the same original accounting workspace. That connection makes the installation maintainable after the first successful payment.

### The customer's complete operating task

The merchant's resource receipts and an implementation or service invoice retain their own original records. A paid resource begins with the approved HTTP or MCP intent, selected payment terms, native settlement and complete output. A prepaid allowance continues its original acquired order while later requests consume service units. A separately agreed customer invoice begins with the accepted scope and a reviewed issued document. Its selected Stellar wallet request retains both the invoice-currency value and exact native or issued-asset amount; receiving binds the verified transfer to the same customer obligation. Its receipt allocations and credits determine the dated amount due; a payment plan places that existing amount on agreed collection dates.

The accounting reconciliation retains the actual network, asset, transaction identity and atomic amount. Commercial-currency amounts retain the merchant's explicit valuation and accounting basis. The customer, accountant and receiving engineer can follow the resulting source link without converting an installment, repeated export or imported document status into another purchase.

|Operating stage|Customer and operator result|Original record carried forward|
|  ---  |  ---  |  ---  |
|Agree the source or service|Name the useful request and complete output, or select the accepted implementation/service quotation.|Buyer intent and terms, or original quotation, customer response and accounting customer.|
|Complete and reconcile the Stellar operation|Receive the full result and review the original settlement, independent network verification and delivery.|Native event, network/asset/atomic units, transaction fingerprint, complete result and selected accounting source.|
|Issue and receive customer charges|Review exact invoice amounts, dates and billing identity; record the actual receipt and its effective invoice allocations.|Frozen invoice files, receipt identity, allocation dates and explicit valuation where selected.|
|Continue collections and corrections|Review credits, dated releases, agreed installment editions and the customer's complete statement.|Original invoice/receipt history, schedule basis and every retained customer edition.|
|Receive into the accountant's organisation|Map issued invoices and credits to actual Xero templates, contact names, accounts and tax fields; receive its original returned document results.|Mapping version, immutable package, external document IDs, exact amounts, validation and correction history.|
|Hand over the running operation|Receive the complete saved workspace and its operating sources, reopen it and continue the customer's agreed task.|Original accounting journal, customer files, request identities, encrypted backup and post-backup reconciliation.|

A period close uses the original account, inclusive statement dates and reviewed balance basis. Its preview checks opening balance plus posted movements against the actual closing balance and presents unresolved source or matching work. A retained close contains complete transaction and posting CSVs, original statements, readable reconciliation, editable account JSON, participating customer account exports and the full file/TAR handover. Reopening an affected close and applying a reviewed replacement preserves its earlier downloadable edition.

The [installation guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/e57a359966f093f483a1aa5f4c2dac28566b6a5c/products/merchant-bank-statements/INSTALLATION.md) receives the named [merchant-bank-statements source selection](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/e57a359966f093f483a1aa5f4c2dac28566b6a5c/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/selections/merchant-bank-statements.json) through the original builder and selected runtime profile. The saved **Bank statement reconciliation** Application starts the existing combined service against the original accounting directory. Source and dependency transfer, runtime upgrade and whole-account recovery retain their existing operations. The [complete operator handover](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/e57a359966f093f483a1aa5f4c2dac28566b6a5c/products/merchant-bank-statements/HANDOVER.md) covers the original source, shared payment, remittance, correction and accountant receiving sequence.

The [maintained complete example](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/e57a359966f093f483a1aa5f4c2dac28566b6a5c/products/merchant-bank-statements/EXAMPLE.md) supplies the original private account programme, full OFX/CSV inputs, native payment/refund/correction/close operations and browser receiving. Its returned native result and customer files identify the actual operated edition. For a selected installation, the receiving engineer opens those original sources and saved records, then continues the customer's own period and agreed accounting mappings within the existing deployment and handover scope.

### Customer service close, corrections and complete handover

A recurring-service merchant needs to explain the work performed after a prepaid pass was acquired. Customer statements now carries that whole operating task: maintain the customer and order assignment, retain the native service captures, choose each pass's service period, review the statement, issue the saved cycle and give the customer its complete files. The installed [customer closing workbench](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/de02bd1d960df2cc462d62c1c71f75fee5e95dee/stellar-forge/mcp-merchant-operator/ACCOUNTING_STATEMENT_WORKBENCH.md) and [service-close planner](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/de02bd1d960df2cc462d62c1c71f75fee5e95dee/stellar-forge/mcp-merchant-operator/ACCOUNTING_STATEMENT_SERVICE_PLANNER.md) use the same merchant accounting workspace as the original purchase and service records.

The closing basis is a pair of actual captures for the same immutable pass. Their original capture times, plan revision and entitlement remain visible. The planner groups these sources by customer and pass and shows current, superseded and withdrawn statements, earlier customer assignments, gaps and ambiguous boundaries. Where history gives a single clear next opening and a later closing capture, it offers those sources for review. The operator chooses the exact boundaries and can add several periods for the same pass. Optional purchase-date filters remain separate from the service boundary.

|Operator stage|Decision made in the installed application|Complete result retained|
|  ---  |  ---  |  ---  |
|Customers and service|Review the customer profile, original order assignment and configured native capture imports.|Customer versions, assignment history, exact capture sources and saved requests.|
|Plan service close|Choose customers, passes, opening and closing captures, the completed accounting run and any original statement being corrected.|Explicit source selections, period and lifecycle context, with the current native source identities.|
|Review the plan|Open the full native usage preview and review every selected customer period.|Complete portable plan JSON, readable HTML and CSV; importing that plan restores its actual selections.|
|Prepare the original cycle|Save the customer reviews before issuing the statements.|Frozen native reviews, the saved preparation request and one durable cycle containing all selected rows.|
|Issue and resume|Issue the reviewed rows and continue an interrupted cycle from its saved requests.|Original statement numbers, per-customer progress and complete delivered files as each row finishes.|
|Correct or withdraw|Review a replacement against the original retained statement, or record the withdrawal reason.|Linked statement editions, original files and the current lifecycle history.|
|Customer handover|Group the customer's passes and periods and download its complete available packet.|A readable index, statement and period registers, complete original statement files and saved status snapshots.|
|Independent continuation|Reopen the customer packet or restore the complete private operator cycle.|Usable relative links and original files for the customer; saved reviews and requests for the receiving operator.|


The customer packet keeps each statement and period readable as its own record. A partially completed cycle still produces a useful register of the available statements and the rows awaiting completion. When a correction or withdrawal is recorded later, the operator refreshes the original delivered statements and prepares the updated customer packet. Repeating an export of unchanged files reuses its retained snapshot; earlier packets preserve the state they contained at delivery. The complete cycle archive carries the operator's saved work for a restart or handover.

The service statement retains the original purchase amounts and measured allowance activity in their own fields. A separately issued invoice, native payment receipt or agreed installment continues through its existing financial record. Customer closing makes those continuing service records inspectable alongside the useful paid output, while the original purchase register supplies its network, transaction and atomic amount.

For a recurring-service operator, the result is a repeatable close: identify the customer and purchased service, explain the activity since the previous close, deliver the statement, and preserve the records needed to answer a later question or correct the period. Staff can continue an interrupted close from its saved cycle and prepare a complete customer handover from the statements already delivered.

For a commissioned customer, the workorder identifies the actual merchant workspace and native capture sources, customer/order mapping, intended service cadence, receiving staff and complete customer output. The existing merchant-resource package covers the selected source and identity adaptation; authority and handover covers the next operator and correction workflow; production recovery covers the complete state and customer-file restoration. This makes continuing customer service a concrete operating outcome within the existing six-package implementation.

The financial workflow provides their operating foundation; the grant allocation applies once to an actual customer adaptation and its technical receiving.

## Wholesale order commissioning and complete ERP receiving

A wholesaler needs a supplier or customer feed to become the intended ERP order, with the original attachments, exact quantities and prices, and a way to reconcile partial processing or later corrections. The complete Metasfresh commissioning product carries that workflow from original intake through operator review, target reconciliation, reporting and independent receiving. Its source is merged in private Commons PR35577, at `35ae501bdc454284637c46725ba47c2293e374dd`; the original company workorder and delivery retain its commercial owner and source custody. This is an implementation candidate; the original contact form has not been submitted and no company email has been sent.

**One complete operating task.** An operator imports the complete feed and attachments, reviews exact-number mappings and the selected source edition, prepares order candidates, and explicitly authorizes processing against the selected target. Read-only allocation and order reconciliation then preserves what the native target actually returned. Attributed corrections create later reviewed editions; reversal coverage retains the affected original work. The browser and CLI expose the same operating history, reports, folder delivery, full backup/restore, and case-handoff export. Original source, requested processing, observed target state and receiving acknowledgment remain separately inspectable.

**Observed result and remaining commissioning.** All 44 complete source files, totaling 464,818 bytes, were read back after merge. Actual local Python/Node, HTTP, installed-build, source-to-report, folder-delivery, two-backup, restore and reopen checks passed. There were **zero Metasfresh target calls**: no customer feed, target or credentials was supplied. The target tenant, original business input, responsible reviewer and receiving engineer are selected in the commissioning agreement before native target acceptance. Source and customer packages remain private; this application describes their capabilities and operating evidence without redistributing those files or treating them as a new public Stellar release.

**The proposed workshare.** The original prepared offer is **USD 12,600 for 96 hours over 15 active business days**: USD 3,150 for agreed scope/start, USD 6,300 for accepted native commissioning, and USD 3,150 for complete receiving. It remains a proposed offer with its original company owner; customer agreement, start, invoices and collections are unset. Its complete local product supplies the foundation for the customer's actual feed mapping, target configuration, reviewed processing, corrections and receiving procedure.

**Effort and cash remain tied to that workorder.** At the application's USD 95/hour assumption, 96 hours allocates **USD 9,120 to labor and leaves USD 3,480 before other costs**. A 25% effort increase gives 120 hours / USD 11,400, leaving USD 1,200 before other costs; labor-only break-even is approximately 132.63 hours. The first USD 3,150 installment would cover approximately 33.16 modeled hours only if actually collected. These are planning comparisons, not incurred cost or received cash. This proposal is separate from the original agency/provider groups, the groundwater proposal and the existing dated portfolio scenarios. Actual source repair, correction, customer waiting and receiving effort inform its agreed schedule and final delivery cost.

**Future Stellar installation in the existing six packages.** A funded selection would name the commissioning payer, authorized ERP/source owner, resource merchant, independent buyer and receiving engineer. It would select a specific publishable order/allocation report or agreed service result, its private versus delivered files, customer purpose and later-use trigger. The existing merchant HTTP or MCP path would then bind that resource to its reviewed network, asset, atomic price and original buyer request. T1 covers the selected source/runtime and consumer mapping plus authority and handover; T2 covers two-facilitator use and recovery of the original paid operation; T3 covers production rollout, recurring useful results and independent restore/support. That is future customer-specific Stellar engineering within the existing six packages. The private generic ERP implementation is not billed again to the grant, and this proposed workshare adds no purchase, independent merchant/buyer, mainnet deployment or collected revenue to the existing totals.
