## External buyer onboarding and study-operations commissioning

The actual Veridex invitation and MedStar technical-partner referral define two concrete implementation tasks. The first concerns an external Stellar buyer; the second concerns an adjacent study and reporting workflow. Their original proposed commercial terms, software capabilities and customer roles are set out below.

### Veridex: an external buyer's first complete operation

### The observed need

In the original October 11 conversation, Emmanuel explained that Veridex already has a conformance suite covering exact payments and settlement. He invited the existing SF88 buyer CLI into the testnet cohort to identify third-party findings and operator UX friction, with endpoint details to follow alignment. That is a concrete need for an external buyer to connect, understand the offered operation and recover a usable result. It is not a request to duplicate the provider's conformance suite.

Bryce's controlling follow-up at 15:23:17 UTC proposes **$1,500 fixed over five business days** for one mutually agreed Veridex `stellar:testnet` exact-payment route. It follows the earlier open-collaboration note and retains route-specific configuration, bounded SF88 adaptation, a reproducible original challenge/approval/response/settlement flow, onboarding/runbook and one agreed acceptance review. Delivery begins after agreed scope and acceptance criteria, received payment and endpoint/access availability. A reciprocal alternative needs written deliverables, usable benefits, timing and usage rights commensurate with the contribution. The latest original thread contains no returned endpoint, selected account or agreement.

The human invitation is therefore evidence of a specific external integration problem. The commercial terms remain a proposal. It supplies no independent customer purchase, paid implementation revenue or selected grant participant.

### The complete unit of work

This table describes the offered work, not a completed Veridex operation. The demonstration already available to a reviewer is the retained HPD paid-query operation. It proves the buyer's existing complete-result and receiving foundation. The Veridex route must have its own original endpoint, request, response and settlement before it can be reported as operated.

For the grant, this is a useful commissioning pattern for T1's customer adaptation and T2's same-service compatibility. The exact route, merchant, buyer, payer and receiving operator still come from the selected installation. Veridex's participation does not by itself select those roles or replace the requirement that the same useful service operate through both testnet facilitators.

**Original evidence:** business-account thread `1a12b2cca0d62069`; human invitation `1a12b7fe875fca98`, October 11 at 15:06:02 UTC; controlling SENT reply `1a12b8fa66d358d1`, 15:23:17 UTC. The original four messages were read directly. Correspondence stays with Bryce and its existing sender.

### MedStar / HealthLab: from study exports to an inspectable comparison

### The actual task and relationship

MedStar's [published Sovereign Execution project](https://healthit.gov/interoperability/investments/leap/2026-leap-in-health-it-projects) includes taxonomy-based shadow human-factors review against baseline workflows. In the actual October 12 reply, its investigator identified HealthLab as the technical partner and said she had shared the proposal. Bryce's approved follow-up asks to agree a defined implementation workshare with that technical lead.

The proposed unit remains **one installation, one study workflow, up to two agreed export families and one report/receiving format, for $12,000 in three $4,000 milestones over twenty business days after the agreed inputs and access are ready**. The current original conversation has no accepted scope, delivery dates, supplied study records, payment or Stellar-use agreement. The customer’s current manual effort and preferred replacement workflow have not been measured; the public project and our proposed integration are the sources of the workflow below.

The merged Study Operations Workspace and complete integration handover implement the adjoining task: import complete exports, select their interpretation, assign and adjudicate human review, compare the intended populations, and deliver the report with the state another operator needs to reopen it. The study owner defines the protocol and decisions; the technical partner defines the Bridge and export interfaces.

This creates a precise acceptance walkthrough for the proposed workshare: the receiving operator follows one agreed source export through its mapping, reviews and adjudicates selected actions, reads the paired population, receives the frozen report and reopens the same work. A later export, reviewed protocol change or completed review period supplies a reason to produce a new report edition. Actual frequency, time saved and willingness to pay remain to be established with the client.

The software keeps different evidence in its own role. An original Task is a resource snapshot. A trace event is an observed event. A Consent object and a human authorization decision are separate. Native Solid access results describe the actual configured server permission observation; they do not supply a patient's authorization. The application records study operations and does not execute patient care.

### How this evidence improves the grant's delivery case

The two examples answer different questions. Veridex's human invitation identifies an external Stellar buyer integration and onboarding task. MedStar's referral identifies the real technical-partner relationship for a defined study/report workshare, while the implemented application demonstrates how its original data, decisions and receiving can stay together. No patient-data publication, paid study service or institutional wallet commitment is proposed as an agreed MedStar action here.

The existing six packages provide the development allocation: customer source/runtime and receiving adaptations in T1; same-service testnet integration and deployed payment/delivery recovery in T2; production deployment, recurring mainnet use and independent maintenance in T3. The existing $38,000, 400 hours and 150-day plan remain unchanged. Any selected adaptation is assigned once to the grant or to the original commercial workshare. Already implemented general study software and uncommissioned sales work are not billed again as prospective Stellar engineering.

Useful measurement follows the actual customer operation. Retain the named operator and task, the selected input and complete output, active integration or review effort, actual corrections, receiving result and later source/request that creates a distinct new task. Keep purchased request counts beside completed parent tasks. A repeated file read, source move or resumed delivery continues its original result. The original SCF cohort model owns the independent operator, testnet/mainnet and repeat-purchase accounting.

## A2A analytical services: complete agent work, merchant delivery and customer receiving

An organisation commissioning an analytical service needs a useful operation that its staff and agent applications can repeat. A reporting team may select a new source edition, run an approved query over every observation, receive complete tables and reports, and hand the working analysis to another engineer. The merchant needs an exact result to publish, native payment terms and a recoverable release. The buyer needs the complete acquired output in its own application.

The installed A2A analytical product joins those tasks through one source selection. It contains the original Python Analysis Workspace, an analytical A2A service, a standard receiving client, the merchant Agent workspace, the original SF30 seller and SF82 release integration, and complete customer receiving commands. Its normal `a2a-analysis` product selection follows the maintained source builder and runtime installer. [Complete installed product](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/9106f038471ba9435f9600ccf5a090d97b6c84f4/products/a2a-analysis/README.md)

### Accountable customer operation

A commissioned installation starts with the actual source and decision the customer needs. Its workorder names the commissioning payer, source owner, analytical service operator, merchant publishing the result, independent buyer and receiving engineer. One organisation may fill more than one role; the service's configuration and commercial agreement retain each authority.

The workorder defines the complete selected source edition, field and time meaning, authorised use and redistribution, saved query or report revision, permitted parameter inputs, full output formats, output limits, expected receiving application and acceptance owner. It identifies the priced unit: for example, one reviewed complete monthly report edition or a named result package. The later reporting period, changed source or distinct approved query supplies the reason for another purchase. Source licence, upstream service access and engineering fees remain recorded with that customer's agreement.

The analytical host captures selected saved queries and report definitions from its original workspace. A caller receives the procedures available to its configured principal. The captured selection retains the actual workspace and view identities, saved SQL or report revision and original parameter text. The customer application can therefore follow which source and procedure produced a delivered result. A deliberate source or procedure change receives a new reviewed selection while earlier task history remains available. [Analytical service and procedure authority](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/9106f038471ba9435f9600ccf5a090d97b6c84f4/stellar-forge/a2a-analysis-agent/README.md)

### Source to complete result

The customer first registers the original acquisition, source document or received dataset in the Analysis Workspace, reviews its projection, imports the selected edition and saves the useful query or report. Its existing Python engine owns those source, SQL, report and export operations. The A2A service connects that application to the official A2A JavaScript SDK 1.3.0 and its original task persistence and event processing. The host selects stable principals, permitted procedures and environment-supplied credentials. [Installed operating flow](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/9106f038471ba9435f9600ccf5a090d97b6c84f4/products/a2a-analysis/OPERATING.md) · [Pinned official SDK source](https://github.com/a2aproject/a2a-js/tree/29417a5bb4038f804f310ce4fffd267a9375aa90)

The merchant operator captures the real Agent Card, reviews its selected interface, saves the exact request and sends a catalogue or selected-procedure message. The task retains its original request, message, context and native job identities before effects. The operator can read or subscribe to the same task, reopen its saved state and continue an interrupted result. The browser retains pending request bytes and drafts; a delayed reply cannot silently substitute another project's selection. [Merchant Agent workspace](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/9106f038471ba9435f9600ccf5a090d97b6c84f4/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/a2a/OPERATOR.md)

Query tasks return the selected complete CSV, JSONL and SQLite exports, the original manifest and an analytical record. Report tasks return the selected full JSON, HTML and CSV ZIP outputs with their original report and publication identities. Full-query completion is required; a preview row limit does not define the delivered population. Configured output limits produce an explicit failed task when the selected complete output cannot fit. When caller parameters are allowed, their original JSON text reaches Python unchanged, preserving integer values that a JavaScript number conversion could alter. [Complete native file contract](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/9106f038471ba9435f9600ccf5a090d97b6c84f4/stellar-forge/a2a-analysis-agent/README.md#complete-customer-files)

Complete-result review binds every retained output to its original Task or Message part position and artifact identity. Inline text, data and raw files are checked against their original bytes. A configured URL output retains the selected URL and observed complete transfer. A receiver rejects missing, duplicated or extra outputs even if a packet claims to be complete. The reviewed result can then become a named immutable edition with its original filenames, media types, byte counts, hashes and task lineage. [Result receiving and exact output population](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/9106f038471ba9435f9600ccf5a090d97b6c84f4/products/a2a-analysis/RECEIVING.md)

### Native payment and release authority

A2A supplies the upstream task and result interface. The merchant publishes the reviewed frozen result through the existing SF30 seller, which retains the network, asset, recipient, integer amount, challenge, verification and settlement records. The existing buyer controls approval, signing and aggregate spending. Its acquired file stays bound to that original paid publication.

The original SF82 release engine owns staging, activation, draining of accepted requests and rollback. An operator reads the current generation before applying the selected release change. An earlier acquired result and its terms remain inspectable after a later release. The Applications integration opens the same retained merchant workspace from its selected installed runtime and private connection configuration. [Merchant publication and release operation](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/9106f038471ba9435f9600ccf5a090d97b6c84f4/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/a2a/OPERATOR.md) · [Installed product commands](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/9106f038471ba9435f9600ccf5a090d97b6c84f4/products/a2a-analysis/README.md#product-commands)

A settled purchase, a completed upstream task, a complete customer file and an accepted business handover have their own records. Funded receiving must join the approved paid request, native transfer, exact output and customer acceptance. The current A2A commissioning source includes an explicitly labelled `CHALLENGE_ONLY` publication exercise; its `verified: false` and `settled: false` values remain visible. That exercise adds no paid purchase to the existing register. [Original commissioning source](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/9106f038471ba9435f9600ccf5a090d97b6c84f4/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/a2a/receiving/commission.mjs)

### Installation, recovery and independent handover

The receiving engineer builds one immutable source commit through the original distribution builder with `--selection a2a-analysis`. The original runtime installer receives the builder's actual archive and SHA-256, selects both `a2a` and `a2a-analysis` features, installs their shared SDK once and checks the actual SQLite binding. The installed source includes the analytical Python package, merchant browser, typed clients, CLI, systemd service and explicitly selected Nginx configuration. The receiving host supplies its own private data directories, credentials, HTTPS origin and service ownership. [Build and installation](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/9106f038471ba9435f9600ccf5a090d97b6c84f4/products/a2a-analysis/OPERATING.md#1-build-and-install-the-selected-source)

The unified `a2a-product` command forwards unchanged arguments to the original runtime, workspace, archive, agent, merchant and receiving modules. The Python workspace entry selects that installed source and Node executable and waits for the original Python owner to finish. A runtime upgrade retains its source and dependency comparison and uses the existing release and rollback controls. Both analytical and merchant components resolve the same selected runtime. [Unified source entry](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/9106f038471ba9435f9600ccf5a090d97b6c84f4/products/a2a-analysis/cli.mjs) · [Python owner entry](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/9106f038471ba9435f9600ccf5a090d97b6c84f4/products/a2a-analysis/python-command.mjs)

The customer receives the type of working material its agreement requires:

|Delivered work|Original receiving operation|What the customer retains|
|  ---  |  ---  |  ---  |
|Analytical task and files|`a2a-product receive`|Agent Card, exact message, original task snapshots and every complete output file|
|Frozen purchased result|`a2a-product merchant inspect-result`|Reviewed edition, native task lineage and exact original output bytes|
|Editable merchant project|`a2a-product merchant receive`|Source review, project revisions, result editions, publications and named handoffs|
|Complete analytical workspace|`a2a-product archive receive`|Original database, retained sources, saved queries, reports and workspace identity|


Receiving the same packet reuses its saved result. A later compatible project carries its own history and earlier named handoffs; an older or divergent packet is identified against the current work. The receiving operator selects its own live host connection before making further upstream requests. Historical inspection and downloads remain bound to the selected revision. The analytical archive receiver checks the complete original members, resumes its own retained staging operation when necessary and publishes the restored workspace through the original engine. [Complete customer receiving guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/9106f038471ba9435f9600ccf5a090d97b6c84f4/products/a2a-analysis/RECEIVING.md)

Recovery preserves the original operation. Losing a receiving stream leaves the service's background task persistence active. A service restart reopens the same task database, procedure selection and native job IDs. Repeated cancellation reconciles the saved native cancellation intent. The final handover retains actual failed, interrupted and unresolved outcomes alongside completed work, so a receiving engineer can finish the identified step. [Task, restart and cancellation contract](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/9106f038471ba9435f9600ccf5a090d97b6c84f4/stellar-forge/a2a-analysis-agent/README.md#resume-and-cancellation)

### Customer commissioning calendar and complete useful jobs

The fourteen-day mainnet target needs an explicit customer calendar. On an ordinary Monday–Friday schedule without holidays, two buyers making one useful purchase each per business day produce twenty purchases in fourteen calendar days. The proposed commissioning calendar reaches thirty through fifteen independently useful jobs per buyer: ten complete source-period extracts and five separate reconciliation or reporting decisions. Both proposed merchant installations serve both buyers. The customer workorder must replace the relative dates, source periods and roles with actual customer selections before this plan can be used.

The [complete customer commissioning specification](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/33dfb64798f5316a586c165d4d7591de972ca4e2/stellar-forge/developer-site/A2A_CUSTOMER_COMMISSIONING.md) and [thirty-job register](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/33dfb64798f5316a586c165d4d7591de972ca4e2/stellar-forge/developer-site/a2a-customer-commissioning.json) name each job's purpose, period, complete output and receiving role. Buyer A's additional jobs cover new or missing observations, late corrections, asset coverage, metadata/status changes and a correction decision register. Buyer B's additional jobs deliver distinct two-period briefs, a source-quality publication, a complete first-workweek report, a selected-cohort report and a complete two-workweek publication. These are prospective customer adaptations to approved saved queries/reports; customer identities, procedure IDs, source licenses, prices, signers and receiving people remain unselected.

For each actual job, the receiving record joins the original customer approval, priced request, native settlement, A2A task, merchant request, full output byte identities and SF82 release/edition to the named receiver's decision. Useful customer jobs, priced requests, native settlements and complete received tasks are counted separately. Retries, reconnects, resumed work, several formats for one result and unnecessary repeat purchases do not create additional useful jobs. The existing development reference and team testnet baseline remain separately attributed.

The appendix preserves the existing $38,000-equivalent request, 400-hour allocation, 150-day programme and milestone definitions. Its remaining customer work fits once into the existing six funded packages, or into a separately commissioned workorder where applicable. Already completed reusable source is the selected starting component. The current manuscript and installation owners approve the actual calendar and accountabilities; this prospective plan records no executed customer outcome or payment.

## Municipal source operations, service reporting and reviewed GIS delivery

Municipal software teams need to carry service requests from their original public system into operational review, performance reporting, GIS allocation and the receiving team's work-order intake. [Connected Bits](https://connectedbits.com/) describes integrations with CRM, GIS, asset and work-order systems and supervisor map/list workflows. Our municipal product makes that complete handoff a reusable service candidate for the existing Stellar merchant architecture.

### Present operating product and source meaning

The merged [Open311 GIS installation](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/6dfd31f9ff239efa9695af2b80a3e506c4e0a7b8/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/open311/gis/INSTALL.md) selects three applications through `open311-gis`: municipal source operations, service performance and GIS handoff. Their browser, installed CLI, typed clients and merchant tools operate the same retained workspaces. Each complete handover carries its original inputs, saved decisions and editable history.

The collector saves a fixed creation or update interval, exact provider filters and all observed source editions. It follows declared pages or refines capped windows, retaining the complete parent and child responses and any unresolved interval. The reporting application selects those immutable collections, a creation period, observation cutoff, named status mappings and a versioned calendar/target profile. Source-provided expected dates remain distinct from the operator's target policy. GIS then imports the complete collection or reporting package, prepares GeoPackage, GeoJSON, CSV or editable JSON, receives analyst changes, compares them with the original source and current assignment, and saves an explicit supervisory decision. A reviewed dispatch maps approved assignments to the receiving system's chosen columns.

These meanings matter to the customer. [Boston's provider](https://311.boston.gov/open311/docs) publishes created-date and changed-record filters, page limits and a ten-request-per-minute allowance. A changed-record feed retains that population; it cannot stand in for all requests created during the same interval. Source closure notes describe the original case disposition. The operator's assignment, due date and dispatch remain separate decisions. Helsinki's native processing statuses and the source's expected date retain their original values. Records without a valid geographic point remain in the working files and receiving history.

The retained Boston source contains an 84-request creation interval, the same population obtained as 40 + 40 + 4 original pages, an empty update interval and a separate 21-request update interval. The earlier basic Helsinki operation completed original capture, review, complete file delivery and independent receiving/reopening. The [original GIS format operation](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/public-commons-sprint-2026/blob/1f45ac52b20f60bb829c2df2c693666847a463aa/operations/open311-gis-8e5f-20261012/format-interchange-result.json) completed four-format round trips over two constructed interoperability cases; a real SQLite analyst edit produced a proposal, accepted decision and dispatch. The complete original-city collection, reporting, GIS, browser and customer-receiving programme is the current engineering continuation. These product results provide a concrete foundation for prospective installation work.

### Customer installation and useful recurring service

We prepared two complete municipal workshares. The sent SocietyWorks workshare proposes **GBP 6,800 / 64 hours / ten active business days** for commissioning: one source endpoint, up to three service groups, two source windows, one report, one receiving environment, two review rounds and an operator walkthrough. The sent Connected Bits workshare proposes **USD 8,400 / 64 hours / ten active business days** for a partner scope covering one installation, original historical/updated reconciliation, reporting and complete engineering handover. Its original company source packet retains the first delivery failure and corrected delivery together. These are prospective commercial installations; the selected grant cohort remains the existing two-merchant, two-buyer plan.

A commissioned service would sell a useful recurring operation: a defined source-period report, changed-case review or reviewed allocation package that the customer needs in its own workflow. Before implementation, the installation workorder names the commissioning payer, accountable merchant, independent buyer, receiving analyst/supervisor and receiving engineer. The source publisher and these commercial roles are recorded separately. The chosen result retains its exact source generation, query and period, reporting profile or handoff edition, output formats and complete receiving interface.

The buyer approves the original merchant's selected Stellar network, asset, recipient and integer atomic amount for that operation. The existing merchant/buyer architecture then joins the approved request, independently observed settlement and complete customer result. Large file continuation, reopening an acquired report and restoring the same workspace continue the original purchase. A later purchase must provide a distinct useful period, source edition or business request. City response bodies and private analyst comments stay in their governed application storage; native payment records carry the original financial and service references.

## OpenLineage service operations and complete customer receiving

The [OpenLineage operations product](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/1b1f756587619d21cab44f627f5d4e9b4fa6ad72/products/openlineage/OPERATING.md) supplies a working source, review and service-level application for a commissioned pipeline operation. Its complete service-level successor is merged in [PR339](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/pull/339), source `1b1f756587619d21cab44f627f5d4e9b4fa6ad72`: 67 maintained application files, including the provider, and 66 files in the portable application. The browser desk, CLI, typed client, direct MCP tools and managed merchant tools share the same workspace and recorded decisions. This is an existing product foundation for a selected installation within the common six funded packages.

### The customer task and commercial roles

A data platform, specialist agency or internal analytics team needs to know whether the pipelines supplying a recurring business output completed within the agreed interval, which original observations support that conclusion, and who resolved an exception. Its receiving analyst also needs the useful report and enough retained source to explain or correct it later. The commissioned installation joins that task to the customer's actual pipeline, operating team and buyer application.

The workorder names the commissioning payer, merchant controlling the authorized source, buyer acquiring the selected useful output, receiving analyst and maintaining engineer. One organization may commission the integration while another operates the source. TokenJunkieLabs' implementation fee belongs to that workorder; the merchant's paid service has its own reviewed output and payment terms.

A suitable paid unit is a complete service review for an agreed pipeline population, source edition and observation time: the saved service-level assessment, selected dataset-quality evaluations, reasoned findings, relevant original records and the agreed report or editable handover. A new reporting period, changed source edition or fresh analysis request creates a reason for the buyer to return. The output definition includes all selected jobs and datasets, service targets, metric or assertion rules, reporting cadence and treatment of late, missing and invalid observations. It names the exception owner and the response commitment, so the merchant and buyer can decide whether the complete task was delivered. A change in dataset population, producer integration or response service becomes a reviewed change to that commercial scope.

T1 connects that selected output to the maintained merchant resource and buyer workflow. It implements the exact HTTP or MCP request, public output mapping, approved network, asset, recipient, atomic amount, entitlement and receiving destination. The buyer reviews the saved request and complete output scope before settlement. The existing Stellar payment and fulfillment components carry that commissioned operation through payment, full result and customer receiving.

### Operate the entire source-to-decision task

1. **Receive the original producer observations.** Select the authorized pipeline population and retain the actual OpenLineage JSON, event array, NDJSON or gzip body. The product includes Python and Java producer entry points and settings generated from the current workspace connection. Operator and producer credentials have distinct roles. The intake retains the original body, source identity and namespaced jobs, runs, datasets and facets; continuation preserves the original operation after an interrupted reply.
2. **Save the service policy and its responsibility.** In **Service levels → Policies**, select the exact namespace and job name, including a job whose first observation is still expected. Record the operational title, owner, effective instant and optional runbook. Choose completion freshness, observed execution duration or failure observations and their time window. Every edit creates a policy version with its prior values and explanation. The operator can inspect the complete history before applying a later target.
3. **Assess a defined observation.** Choose an explicit observation time and the current source selection or a saved edition, then preview. The evaluator uses the original lineage projection. It excludes observations after the selected time, retains invalid-time diagnostics and exposes missing original START timestamps as unavailable duration. It shows each policy's findings, due and observed times, original source/event references and coverage. Saving retains that exact source selection and policy snapshots. Historical editions and older observation times stay in the assessment history.
4. **Work the exception through its outcome.** An applied current assessment updates the incident desk. The operator assigns an owner, acknowledges the incident and retains the reason. A newly retained original event can establish the missing completion; reassessment records that the condition has cleared, and the operator resolves the incident. Acceptance of an active condition is a separate recorded decision. Policy changes and later observations retain the earlier findings, decisions and assessments.
5. **Deliver the useful report and selected originals.** The application exports JSON, CSV and printable HTML with policy versions, original references and incident history. A saved assessment download contains its exact selected record and snapshots. A report combines that selected assessment with the current policy records and incident history; this scope is visible beside the report controls. The commissioned output mapping chooses the required records and formats, binds them to the reviewed paid unit, and carries every agreed file to the buyer's actual destination.
6. **Hand over an editable installation.** A complete workspace export carries its original objects, editions, policy history, assessments, incidents, operation journal and the portable application. The receiving engineer opens that same workspace, inspects the prior decision and continues its work. The application keeps the workspace identity across server instances and preserves the original request body and operation ID when recovering an interrupted save. A later source or policy change becomes a new reviewed action.

The [service-level operating contract](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/1b1f756587619d21cab44f627f5d4e9b4fa6ad72/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/openlineage-workspace/SERVICE_LEVELS.md) describes the evaluator, versioned decisions, reports and full receiving behavior. The [operator desk guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/1b1f756587619d21cab44f627f5d4e9b4fa6ad72/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/openlineage-workspace/SERVICE_LEVELS_OPERATOR.md) gives the complete browser workflow, connection recovery, conflict review and source downloads. The [original source contract](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/1b1f756587619d21cab44f627f5d4e9b4fa6ad72/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/openlineage-workspace/SOURCE_CONTRACT.md) identifies the upstream producer semantics and retained examples.

### Dataset quality commissioning and recurring customer review

The Quality desk extends the same operating workspace to rules over producer-reported measurements and assertions. Its complete source, operator guide and original receiving programme are supplied for the cumulative application. The commissioned review combines these decisions with the service policies and incident history under the same agreed pipeline edition and receiving destination.

### Establish the customer's operating selection

Commissioning starts with the pipeline engineer's complete original event files or the configured producer endpoint. The operator identifies the exact dataset namespaces and names, original job and run keys, accepted producer configuration, and the workspace in which the customer will operate. The commissioning record also names who may send producer events, who may save staff decisions, who receives the customer package and where that receiving installation is kept. The existing application supports separate producer and operator credentials and preserves the original workspace identity across ordinary server restarts.

The first saved edition establishes the customer's source selection. The operator inspects the supplied facet history and the original source locations, agrees the useful dataset rules, and records the selected rule versions. A dataset in a different namespace remains a distinct dataset. Dataset-level observations and observations attached to a particular run's input or output retain their separate scopes. The review can therefore explain precisely which producer observation supports a finding and which source selection the customer accepted.

The customer-facing desk provides four connected screens: Observations, Rules, Evaluation and Decisions. It also uses the application's original source inspector and saved-request recovery panel. An engineer can open the source behind a finding, review its full original facet, and continue an interrupted action using the original request identity. The same actions are available through the maintained CLI, typed client, direct MCP and managed merchant connection.

### Turn reported observations into a retained decision

The observation review preserves the producer's reported values and source context. A completed run, a failed assertion and that assertion's warning severity remain separate facts in the review. An omitted measurement stays unreported; a reported zero keeps its original meaning. The original containing record remains available when the producer uses a source contract that the adapter cannot interpret.

An operator can save a metric rule for an exact reported field, or a named assertion rule for the exact assertion and optional column. Each rule identifies the dataset, facet scope, severity, enabled state and treatment of missing observations. Metric comparisons use finite thresholds or an inclusive range. A revised or disabled rule retains its earlier versions, and an existing evaluation retains the versions used to produce it.

Evaluation previews bind to the currently selected workspace revision, edition, dataset and run. Saving from the browser also binds the exact source-selection and rule-set hashes returned with the displayed preview. If another action changes the selection or revision, the operator reviews the current state before saving the retained intent. A saved evaluation preserves its full findings, expected and actual values, original event and observation identities, source locations and selected rules.

The operator then records a reasoned disposition against a specific finding in that saved evaluation: open, investigating, accepted or resolved. Each update preserves earlier decisions and the original finding. A subsequent producer event supports a subsequent evaluation, so the receiving engineer can inspect both the earlier result and the later correction. Supporting files can accompany that history through the application's existing complete result-attachment workflow.

The recurring deliverable includes the complete selected originals, applicable dataset-rule versions, saved evaluations, reasoned findings and reports alongside the service-level assessment. JSON retains the structured evaluation; CSV carries its findings into ordinary spreadsheet work; HTML presents the review in a readable report. The editable handover retains the earlier source editions, rules, findings and decisions so the receiving engineer can inspect a correction and continue the next review.

### Publish the customer's analysis lineage

The original Analysis Workspace now carries retained imports, saved SQL queries, complete query exports and workbooks into an OpenLineage publication workflow. The customer inspects their dependency graph, saves and reviews the publication plan, publishes through the maintained collector client and reopens the same request after an interrupted reply. This connects the analytical result used by the customer to its original source and transformations.

The complete event, collector receipt and readable HTML/ZIP handovers remain with the original workspace backup and restore history. A receiving engineer can inspect the proposed lineage, review what the collector returned and continue from the retained request. ## Current alternatives, commercial units and customer value

The customer buys a recurring task: an authorised source, its complete useful result in the receiving application, and an installation another operator can maintain. Payment, discovery, deployment and recovery products already provide substantial parts of that workflow. The six funded packages develop the selected customers’ remaining source mapping, receiving, deployment and maintenance work.

[ApiCharge’s public preview](https://apicharge.com/) deploys models on selected infrastructure and exposes typed paid parameters; its [route grants](https://apicharge.com/Documentation/core-concepts.html) retain purchased quality of service when later prices change. [MPP Router](https://www.mpprouter.dev/llms.txt) publishes Stellar x402 v2 service access, signed asynchronous-job polling and a 24-hour response cache keyed by request ID. [Nirium’s maintained SDK and seller source](https://github.com/nirium-protocol/nirium) supplies payment clients, seller middleware and MCP. Our comparison measures the additional work needed to carry a complete recurring customer task across source editions, every required page or file, the receiving application, fulfillment/accounting and independent maintenance.

Provider selection starts with the customer’s authorised source and least expensive suitable access. [Blockscout](https://docs.blockscout.com/devs/x402-payments) offers key-based billing and Base x402 access to the same data. [Routescan](https://routescan.io/docs/plans-and-limits/api-keys-and-pricing) provides free keyless and registered access as well as paid plans; coverage and throughput must match the selected task. [Tenderly’s Free offering](https://tenderly.co/pricing) is browser-only, with API service in its commercial offering. The workorder records the chosen account/plan, rights, source scope, billing interval and actual provider and support costs.

The existing $38,000 / 400-hour / 150-day programme measures customer value through two independent merchant and buyer installations, the same useful service through two testnet facilitators, recurring mainnet purchases and an independent maintainer’s handover. For each installation, compare the original task and installed task on equivalent source and output: active effort, correction effort, elapsed time to useful output, actual incremental cost and the later customer request that led to repeat use. Assign each performed adaptation once to its existing funded package or separately commissioned workshare.

## Customer value and delivery economics

Evaluate the complete task and its recurrence. Let F be the one-time implementation fee, V the customer’s stated value of an hour, H the measured active hours saved per equivalent completed task, N the number of useful repeat tasks, and C the period’s incremental provider, hosting, payment and support cost. The direct labor-value comparison is `N × H × V − F − C`; the effort reduction per task needed to recover the fee is `(F + C) / (N × V)`.

The following planning example assumes twelve monthly tasks and zero entered incremental costs. The two hourly values are explicit scenarios for the customer to replace with its own value; the prior and installed tasks must retain comparable source scope and usable output.

|Implementation fee|Assumed customer hour value|Hours recovered across twelve tasks|Hours per monthly task|
|  ---  |  ---  |  ---  |  ---  |
|$3,600|$75|48.00|4.00|
|$3,600|$125|28.80|2.40|
|$4,800|$75|64.00|5.33|
|$4,800|$125|38.40|3.20|
|$7,200|$75|96.00|8.00|
|$7,200|$125|57.60|4.80|


Enter actual incremental costs before using the comparison for an accepted engagement. At a $4,800 fee and $125/hour value, the year needs 38.4 avoided hours plus another avoided hour for each $125 of incremental cost. Reducing a four-hour monthly task to one hour yields 36 hours a year, so that scenario requires further useful value or a different fee/scope to recover the implementation fee in the first year.

CoCart’s existing proposal is $7,200 for 60 planned hours over fifteen business days. Its proposed partner compensation is 5% of collected initial implementation fees. At full collection, that is $360. Applying the grant’s existing $95/hour planning allocation gives the following commercial sensitivity:

|Planning quantity|Calculation|Amount|
|  ---  |  ---  |  ---  |
|Base work allocation|60 × $95|$5,700|
|Fee remaining after base work|$7,200 − $5,700|$1,500|
|Proposed partner compensation at full collection|5% × $7,200|$360|
|Remaining difference before incremental cost|$7,200 − $5,700 − $360|$1,140|
|Work capacity before incremental cost|($7,200 − $360) / $95|72 hours|
|Additional work that consumes the difference|72 − 60|12 hours|


This is a planning allocation using the existing proposed terms. Actual contributor rates, accepted scope, reusable work, corrections, support and collected payments determine the commercial result. Each further $95 of incremental cost removes one hour from the 72-hour allowance. Assign completed reusable adaptations once between customer work and the remaining prospective grant packages.

The original Installation/Workshare retains the commissioning payer, merchant, buyer, receiving engineer and relationship owner. Its receiving review records the source edition/rights, selected provider plan, agreed paid unit, expected complete pages/files, fee, actual costs and collections, delivery allocation and next useful task. Compare three original operations: initial delivery, the next reporting period or changed source, and a maintainer’s change/recovery. Their full input/output scope, active effort, correction effort and customer acceptance make the next estimate useful.

The installed [Customer task outcomes desk](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/e692ac8cdab0adee3c0bb921cf580ebf7277c128/stellar/scf_2026/sf47_budget_model/workspace/TASK_OUTCOMES.md) supplies the complete comparison for these three operations. Each comparison retains the original and installed method, the customer and receiving team, source population, period, useful task, completion criteria, attempted and completed counts, and the selected customer Installation edition. The operator attaches the original records and identifies which inputs are observed, estimated or mixed.

Record active person-time for source acquisition, processing, correction, receiving and other necessary work. Keep whole-operation elapsed time separately, enter each contributor's applicable hourly rate and every incremental cost in one selected currency, and retain the original price or work source. An entered zero remains zero; an unknown rate leaves that part of the cost incomplete. The result shows the complete entered inputs, the known amounts and the remaining quantities to obtain. This gives the receiving engineer a practical way to include time spent collecting pages, correcting outputs and installing the usable result.

The operator then reviews whether the two methods have comparable scope, output and quality, retaining the reason and conclusion. Equal positive completion counts support a whole-task comparison; differing counts use the per-completed-task comparison. The reviewed edition retains its original plan, Installation and source selections, so later changes to the deployment or grant plan preserve the basis of an earlier result. Enter the resulting measured active-hours difference and the customer's own hour value into the commercial scenarios above, together with the period's actual incremental costs.

A saved comparison can be reopened, revised and delivered with its complete offline report, effort and cost tables, every earlier comparison edition and the original operating case. The receiving engineer imports that complete case, inspects the selected historical edition and continues the same comparison under the current plan. Retained editor drafts and recovery of the original save request support interrupted work. The same customer handover therefore carries the measurement inputs, calculation, human review and editable history needed for the next reporting period or maintenance change.

The original commercial comparison and commissioning source retains the proposed company terms and complete measurement worksheet. The maintained [Grant Operations workspace](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/aef3646aa9d432b671839f5285e705b1b9dbaa0a/products/grant-operations/OPERATING.md), [supplier accounts](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/aef3646aa9d432b671839f5285e705b1b9dbaa0a/stellar/scf_2026/sf47_budget_model/workspace/PAYABLES.md), [account statements](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/aef3646aa9d432b671839f5285e705b1b9dbaa0a/stellar/scf_2026/sf47_budget_model/workspace/STATEMENTS.md) and [installation portfolio](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/aef3646aa9d432b671839f5285e705b1b9dbaa0a/stellar/scf_2026/sf47_budget_model/workspace/PORTFOLIO.md) connect those actual obligations, reviewed cash movements and dated work to the original case and complete receiving.

## Timescale commissioning and complete customer reconciliation

An engineering team can commission a service that turns an existing Timescale commissioning exercise into a complete, reusable customer analysis. The buyer receives the original report, both selected native source populations, a reviewed interpretation of every field, the saved baseline-to-observed comparison, engineering decisions and a portable DuckDB workspace. The useful result is an analysis the customer's engineer can open, explain and continue when the next operating period or corrected source arrives.

**The customer problem.** A historian export and a screenshot of differences leave substantial work for the receiving engineer. They must recover the exact source selection, distinguish a SQL NULL from an empty string, interpret native time and quality fields, decide which records identify the same observation, account for duplicates and preserve the original report behind the result. The maintained Timescale and DuckDB products carry those choices through one operating history. A later reviewer can inspect the complete original population and the decisions that produced the customer report.

**Implemented product.** The complete Timescale customer join is merged in [public PR2422](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/public-commons-sprint-2026/pull/2422) at d8365c0ecbd5bb02bd9f031acd5970a52ae0e9aa and [Merchant Workspace PR359](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/pull/359) at b6d4704d7020a1cf60dc04fb1762aea192928651. The latter contains the 33-file customer integration. Its selected product combines the original Timescale commissioning owner, the existing Python DuckDB customer, paired reconciliation, browser controls, CLI, typed client, merchant and buyer MCP, and managed Applications.

The original Timescale workspace creates the immutable commissioning JSON report with its complete revision chain and native source files. The customer retains that exact file, its filename and source identities in its existing warehouse. Operators inspect all fields, review native types and meanings, import immutable baseline and observed editions, and save a comparison through the existing paired engine. That engine supplies complete row accounting, duplicate groups, engineer decisions, report snapshots and portable customer export. The original customer listener and request journals continue to own the operation. [Complete product and receiving guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/b6d4704d7020a1cf60dc04fb1762aea192928651/products/timescale-customer/OPERATING.md).

Native cells retain their PostgreSQL text, SQL NULL and column OID. Every original field initially maps to a textual representation; an operator can select an exact integer, decimal or time representation through the native review. Roles, meanings, units, null interpretation and time basis travel with the edition. Import retains every original row, including duplicate identifiers. Matching keys and optional time windows belong to the later comparison definition, where the engineer can see their effect on the complete accounting.

**Commissioning and commercial roles.** The workorder names the commissioning payer, source administrator, merchant operator, buyer organization and receiving engineer. A platform or delivery partner can introduce the customer and operate the source while TokenJunkieLabs supplies the agreed source, application, payment and handover engineering. The customer's scope identifies the exact project/report, baseline and observed source IDs, time or operating period, every required output and the decision that the engineer will make with the result. The complete [Timescale commissioning playbook](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/main/products/timescale-customer/COMMISSIONING.md) applies the shared customer-launch process to these native fields and outputs.

The initial commercial scope is one agreed customer environment and one complete commissioning workflow, with the actual source populations, report definitions and recurring task specified in the workorder. Implementation pricing follows its original accepted scope and staffing estimate. The merchant's price for using the resource is a separate term. This separation lets a delivery partner pay for an installation while an independent buyer pays for subsequent useful reports, and preserves the payer, recipient, invoice and actual collection for each arrangement.

**The paid customer unit.** A suitable first deployment prices the whole selected commissioning result: one reviewed report edition, its complete native sources and the agreed receiving output. The installation records the exact source/report identity, request, route or tool arguments, network, asset, recipient, atomic amount and total approved task cost. Where the chosen resource instead charges per page or query, the original purchase records remain separate and the full result retains one parent customer task. Importing or reopening the retained report uses the existing customer operation and creates no new purchase.

The prospective Stellar work connects this concrete resource to the maintained merchant and buyer interfaces. The buyer's approved request and payment operation lead to the original complete report and its native customer receiving. A changed report, period, source contract or independently requested analysis is selected deliberately as later work. The engineer can continue a previously acquired edition while reviewing the new one. The [shared launch playbook](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/main/products/merchant-workspace/CUSTOMER_LAUNCH.md) supplies the installation, financial and cohort interfaces for these choices.

**The complete operating demonstration.** The retained Timescale producer supplies the actual commissioning report. In the original DuckDB customer, the operator retains it, downloads the same complete file, reviews every source field, imports the two immutable editions and saves their pair. The existing browser then carries that pair into reconciliation, where the engineer runs the full accounting, reviews differences, records a decision and saves the report. The native client receives the complete report and source files, and the portable warehouse reopens them with the same selected definitions.

The source includes a complete receiving programme that joins the original browser, MCP owner, comparison and portable warehouse. It retains its full input, operation ID and results so that the same customer work can continue after an interruption. The commissioned demonstration uses the original producer report and the existing customer operation. Its final result supplies the actual report, source, edition, comparison and destination identifiers that the application owner can attach to the product narrative.

**Fit within the existing funded work.** If selected as one of the two merchant installations, this customer's remaining deployment and receiving work occupies the existing six packages:

|Funded package|Timescale customer work and completion|
|  ---  |  ---  |
|T1 merchant-resource integration|Connect the customer's actual source and host; review all source/field meanings; configure the complete paid resource, buyer request and original customer intake; deliver the entire analysis in the customer's warehouse.|
|T1 authority and handover|Have a second accountable operator reopen the installation, perform the agreed source/terms change or withdrawal, and continue the earlier acquired report under its original record.|
|T2 provider and ledger deployment|Operate the same useful commissioning resource through both independently operated facilitators and connect each original purchase, provider and received customer result to the existing cohort.|
|T2 deployed threat response|Deploy the customer-specific monitoring and response; recover an interrupted settled delivery and a merchant delivery failure through the original report, requests and full useful output.|

The programme remains **400 prospective hours / USD 38,000 over 150 days from actual award acceptance**, with the original 80/40/70/50/90/70-hour package allocation. T2 retains at least ten useful testnet purchases in total by two independent buyers over seven consecutive days ending by day 90. T3 retains at least thirty useful mainnet purchases in total by two independent buyers over fourteen consecutive days ending by day 150, with both returning for a distinct purchase on another day. Two merchant organizations and two independently operated facilitators retain their original meaning. Each adaptation is assigned once to its funded package or separately commissioned workorder.

**Learning and repeatable delivery.** The commissioning case records time from the original source selection to a usable report, engineer time spent interpreting fields and resolving differences, time to receive a corrected period, actual installation effort and subsequent support demand. The cohort records distinct completed purchases and whole customer tasks separately, together with their accountable operators, original payment amounts, provider and completion dates. The receiving engineer confirms that the output supports the agreed business decision and continues the same workflow for the next required period. These observations show which source interpretations, customer mappings and operating procedures can be reused in the next paid installation.

## IATI publishing, programme finance and complete customer receiving

An aid-data publisher or its implementation partner can commission one operating workflow that turns the organisation publication and its selected activity portfolios into an editable financial review. The receiving analyst gets the original XML, assessed records, explicit scope, original currency and dates, named decisions, comparison report and the workspace needed for the next edition. A programme officer can explain how the selected activity amounts relate to the organisation's published budget while retaining the original source qualifications.

The same customer workspace also supports a geographic review of the publisher's activity locations. The analyst can connect an exact financial portfolio to its reported places, keep unlocated or invalid records visible, save named findings and deliver a complete editable review with map and data exports. Activity amounts retain their original financial grouping; the application does not divide a budget or transaction across location points.

### Customer task and commercial roles

The workorder identifies the commissioning payer, publisher or source administrator, merchant operator, buyer organisation, financial reviewer and receiving engineer. The publisher selects the authorised organisation and activity sources. The reviewer defines the reporting period and activity coverage. The engineer agrees the complete report and files that must open in the customer's existing application, along with the host, integration and acceptance owner.

The existing AidStream offer gives this installation work a concrete commercial unit: USD 6,400 for 64 planned hours over ten business days, up to three selected publisher organisations and two editions each, one export/API integration, complete organisation budget/document review and corrected XML, two consolidated reviews and portable operator handover. Its two proposed milestones are USD 3,200 each. The original commissioning scope and sent proposal remain the terms of that offer. Financial reconciliation is an additional reusable product capability; its selected customer scope belongs in the corresponding agreed workorder.

This approach also supports the existing consultant proposals in the source record: Data4Development's edition, finance and client-receiving workshare and Zimmerman's native assessment integration. Each company keeps its original conversation, payer and scope. A publishing or implementation partner can introduce the organisation whose recurring reporting task needs the installation.

### Implemented product and financial meaning

The [merged cumulative IATI implementation](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/pull/388) composes organisation planning and document review, activity portfolios, Results, AMP and financial reconciliation into the maintained Merchant Workspace. The complete selected source includes the native engines, browser, CLI, typed client, Merchant MCP tools, Applications bindings, publisher inputs and operating guides. The [financial operating guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/2854a9f5f0d792dd78497228a1d23d9a69305763/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/iati/ORGANISATION_RECONCILIATION.md) defines the complete workflow.

The operator selects one exact saved organisation revision and one or more exact activity-portfolio revisions. The application reads their complete financial registers. Each comparison selects the actual organisation record and individual activity rows and retains the reviewer's coverage statement. Named issue decisions, saved revisions and approval or request-changes reviews remain attached to that definition.

|Financial question|Maintained operating behaviour|
|  ---  |  ---  |
|What is being compared?|Organisation budgets select activity budget records; organisation total expenditure selects activity expenditure transactions. Reporting identity, hierarchy, period, budget type and status remain visible.|
|Which activities and periods are covered?|The comparison records the exact selected rows and its own coverage statement. The operator can explicitly retain an organisation record with no selected activity coverage and its associated finding.|
|How are differing value dates handled?|The default keeps incompatible value-date contexts separate. An explicit nominal comparison preserves both original dates and their qualification while comparing eligible amounts in the same currency.|
|What happens to overlapping or incompatible records?|Original/revised budgets, overlapping periods and incompatible hierarchy contexts retain their native exclusions and reasons. The reviewer can respond to a finding while the calculated eligibility remains visible.|
|What does the customer receive?|Complete HTML, CSV and JSON reports plus a nested-source package carrying the organisation, activity and reconciliation work. A receiving engineer can reopen the selected revision and continue its current case.|


Monetary values remain decimal strings through the browser and typed client. The native engine owns the calculation, and the saved report retains every included or excluded row. A later review is visible in history even when the numerical comparison remains unchanged. These behaviours make the financial conclusion explainable to the receiving analyst.

### Published documents and source review

An analyst reviewing an aid programme needs to trace a financial finding back to the publication that supports it. The [document-evidence workspace](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/3d86d3e30917aad9c34a27718b4bbbc540933334/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/iati/DOCUMENT_EVIDENCE.md) connects that task to the existing organisation and financial applications. It retains the publishing row, literal document URL, dated acquisition, response bytes and named assessment together.

The operator starts from a selected organisation revision and its source or candidate view. Each register row retains the title, category, language, date, URL and correction target. A saved evidence plan identifies the rows, source snapshot and capture limits. The analyst can therefore relate the document to the reporting period and source edition used in the financial comparison.

|Customer operation|Product behaviour|
|  ---  |  ---  |
|Select the published material|Choose an organisation edition and its document rows. Source and candidate views retain their respective snapshots and existing edits.|
|Capture a document|Record the dated request, redirect chain, response status and retained bytes through the native fetcher. An explicitly requested later observation preserves the earlier capture.|
|Review the evidence|Record a named decision for every selected row and the observation supporting it. The reviewer assesses the document's relevance and suitability.|
|Correct a publishing link|Prepare the organisation planner's full correction request, retaining existing source edits and its revision check. Inspect and apply it through the organisation workflow.|
|Compare editions|Inspect changes in document metadata, observations and decisions. Compatible complete bodies support a same-or-changed comparison; an incomplete earlier response keeps its recorded acquisition outcome.|
|Hand over the analysis|Export the source, plan history, requests, observations, response assets, comparisons and reports. A receiving analyst opens that edition and continues it with their own notes.|


Six browser views cover source and document selection, acquisition, review, comparison, handover and receiving. The CLI, typed JavaScript client and Merchant interface operate the same native records. HTML, CSV and JSON outputs support reading and further analysis outside the browser. Each captured body retains its byte representation and content-encoding descriptor.

### Recurring customer work and the purchased output

A commissioned document task identifies the organisation and reporting periods, selected publications, authorized source, output formats, reviewer and receiving application. The engineer connects those sources to the customer's reporting process. The analyst reviews the evidence, resolves publishing errors where appropriate, explains changes between editions and hands over the report with its supporting material.

### Geographic review of the original publisher records

The [Geography product](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/4424e79ea489f3bcec147aed08171f5c27959f98/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/iati/GEOGRAPHY.md) and [operator and typed-client guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/4424e79ea489f3bcec147aed08171f5c27959f98/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/iati/GEOGRAPHY_UI.md) extend the same IATI console, saved source store and Applications entry. A geographic review selects complete publisher editions, exact activity coverage and, when relevant, one saved financial portfolio revision. The publisher's narratives, gazetteer references, administrative areas, original point text, classifications and extension content remain attached to each location.

A valid coordinate is a point that meets the published format, cardinality, CRS and numeric-range rules. It is not independent confirmation that the reported place is geographically correct. The map shows valid reported points on a coordinate graticule. Missing, invalid and unreported positions remain in the register; the application does not invent a centroid or geocode an absent point. Publisher exactness, location class and reach retain their stated meanings. In particular, intended-beneficiary reach and coordinate precision do not establish a financial allocation to that place.

### Operate the saved geography review

1. In Sources, retain the complete publisher XML and its actual publisher, URL, acquisition time, licence and citation. In Geography, name the review and select the original source editions. Choose all activities or an explicit activity list and preferred narrative language. Linking a saved financial portfolio uses that exact portfolio revision's sources and activity selection.
2. Inspect coverage before drawing a conclusion. Read the location register, open a complete source record and inspect its narratives, administrative and gazetteer associations, reported point, classifications and issues. Continue the actual returned page cursor; load the full valid-point set before describing the displayed map as complete. Filters and a partial page do not redefine the full export.
3. Prepare a finding against the exact source and row: accepted, needs-correction or note, with the named reviewer and explanation. Set the whole review to draft, reviewed or needs-correction separately. Save the complete definition against its expected current revision. A finding records the analyst's decision without changing the publisher XML.
4. Open an earlier saved revision to inspect its original selection, report, findings and exports. Prepare changes from the latest revision. Comparing two revisions pairs unchanged source identities automatically; replacement publisher editions require explicit before/after source pairs. Unpaired files remain complete additions or removals, and findings do not silently migrate to another source.
5. If a save response is interrupted, continue the original retained request. The browser keeps its complete input and original request ID before dispatch. A recorded request returns the exact historical result; only an unrecorded request is sent again unchanged. A changed workspace or unrelated pending input stays available for inspection.
6. Export the agreed full deliverables, then receive the packet in the customer's original IATI workspace. The receiver checks every member and source, reconstructs native editions and reports, and preserves the complete original requests and comparison history. The receiving analyst can reopen the imported review and save a further named edition.

The existing authenticated HTTP and typed-client operations cover that same review. The fourteen Merchant methods are state, reviews, review, history, report, request, save, rows, points, compare, comparison, changes, export and receive. They use the configured original workspace alias and retained file carrier; a complete file can be read or received without rebuilding it from interactive pages.
