|  ---  |  ---  |
|T1 merchant-resource integration, 80 hours|Bind the selected publisher editions, financial-review resource and complete reports/package to the customer's HTTP or MCP service and buyer receiving application. The independent buyer opens the agreed full output with its original financial context.|
|T1 authority and handover, 40 hours|Carry a reviewed source/terms change or withdrawal through the installation. A second operator reopens the exact sources and reviews and performs the agreed change.|
|T2 provider and ledger deployment, 70 hours|Configure the same useful review resource through two independent testnet facilitators, joining each approved purchase, transfer and complete output. The existing independent-buyer purchase targets apply.|
|T2 deployed threat response, 50 hours|Operate interrupted settled delivery and merchant-delivery failure with the original request, financial outcome and unfinished receiving work retained. Complete the customer's recovery and operating notifications.|
|T3 mainnet rollout, 90 hours|Deploy the selected production host/network/asset/account configuration and recurring publisher-period workflow, then complete independent buyer use under the existing mainnet cohort targets.|
|T3 production recovery and handover, 70 hours|Restore the original configuration, selected sources, reviewed cases and customer files on the receiving host; reconcile later operations and complete another maintainer's support case.|


The existing 400-hour, USD 38,000, 150-day allocation remains the combined grant programme. Each customer adaptation is assigned once to that programme or its separately commissioned workorder. Completed source engineering supplies the starting product.

The receiving analyst's acceptance is practical: open the full sources and report, explain the selected financial coverage, inspect the original dates and exclusions, make a named review decision, receive the complete work independently and continue with the next agreed edition. The installation records active effort, manual corrections and time to accepted output alongside the shared customer-value and recurring-use measures.

## Product selection, installation and recurring buyer work

**Choose the product for the complete customer task.** An operator starts in [Source Builds](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/4007537fb13f3c6088cf28b153a28293c149b496/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/runtime-workspace/SOURCE_BUILDS.md) with the customer’s useful operation, source and expected output. Command finder exposes the installed commands and their original registrations. The source catalogue searches named products and [matches the complete requested capability basket](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/4007537fb13f3c6088cf28b153a28293c149b496/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/discovery/PRODUCT_REQUIREMENTS.md) against one immutable revision. Product detail and comparison show the included commands, applications, merchant connections, API exports, source components and native requirements. The dependency reader opens the actual committed manifests and supported lockfiles, retaining declared requirements, resolved package versions and unresolved entries. The operator can compare a named selection with the full toolkit and choose the product and adapter groups needed by the receiving application.

**Keep the reviewed source and original installation together.** A [saved product plan](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/4007537fb13f3c6088cf28b153a28293c149b496/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/runtime-workspace/PRODUCT_PLANS.md) retains the task’s purpose, required capabilities, immutable recipe, source inspection and original review/build request. Reopening the same local plan uses its retained source and restores that native identity. Its original controls build the package, retain the archive and prepare the chosen adapter profile. The plan’s Installed runtimes section finds preparation, installation and recovery work using that exact archive SHA-256. Operators select the actual profile when more than one installation uses the package, then open the existing Runtime controls to continue the same work. Command-line and authenticated local API routes expose the same saved plan, installation selection and handoff.

**Prepare the recurring buyer operation.** In the installed [Request Collections workspace](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/68a2ded6c8e24b46bc016ec69b13e3b32927919f/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf88-operator-buyer-cli/collections/AUTHORING.md), the operator authors or imports a reusable request plan. For each request, the operator selects the actual saved provider catalogue, original row and payment alternative, destination, method, arguments and existing buyer operator. A named period resolves the agreed values into stable request identities. Preparation retains the complete original catalogue, selected operator configuration, request body, operation ticket and prepared request files before the collection is created. The review displays the selected work and its existing payment terms. Each prepared period reopens with its retained inputs and the immutable plan revision that defined it.

**Save the customer's dated work.** The same [Installation workspace](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/c912e6ecb56a1f049901401d71f98be6cfd5dbb1/stellar/scf_2026/sf47_budget_model/workspace/INSTALLATIONS.md) retains the commissioning payer, merchant and buyer deployments, selected source records and pinned plan. Its [Customer-use Calendar](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/c912e6ecb56a1f049901401d71f98be6cfd5dbb1/stellar/scf_2026/sf47_budget_model/workspace/CUSTOMER_USE_CALENDAR.md) adds complete tasks: the customer's question, reviewed source period or population, exact request, priced unit, aggregate spending basis, expected whole output and the change that makes later work useful. Select the actual UTC dates, weekdays and closures before expanding a recurring pattern. Review the dated tasks and separate funding groups, then preview and save an immutable Installation edition. A direct purchase group belongs to its stated task; an explicitly prepaid group may fund several useful tasks. A planned group has no invented receipt.

**Operate and return to the same work.** Creating the reviewed period calls the original collection controller. The operator opens that collection and runs the complete task or a selected subset through the existing approval, signer, budget and receiving path. Each selected request keeps its own operator mapping. An interrupted creation resumes the matching original collection with the same retained request files; completed requests and saved results remain available through the original workspace. A later useful reporting period receives its own reviewed period reference. Changed retained inputs or original operator configuration are surfaced in the review before the collection is created.

**Compare planned demand with actual use.** Keep the selected cohort rule and dates fixed while comparing the schedule. Two buyers making one purchase on each of ten included weekdays provide twenty planned purchases in a fourteen-day window. A thirty-purchase T3 plan therefore needs additional distinct useful paid requests from those same selected buyers and both merchants, supported by their work; it cannot be filled by retries or reopening. Several paid pages may complete one parent task. A prepaid acquisition remains one purchase after its first whole accepted output, while subsequent calls retain their allowance-use identities. The calendar projects repeat potential from the first whole useful-result day of each distinct funding group. The original Cohort evaluator determines actual eligibility from its retained first attempt, independently verified transfer and complete accepted output within the window.

**Hand over the original installed product and buyer state.** The selected ready Runtime supplies its original deployment handoff after the native inspector verifies the package source, installed manifest, profile and dependency lock against the saved review. The full export carries the plan, local binding, review, build request, archive and installation identities, original commands, observed installed versions and existing managed-release arguments. A readable HTML, print or Markdown briefing presents that same purpose, capability basket and selected installation to the commissioning payer and receiving engineer. Complete plan receiving retains the originating source and build history while establishing the receiving workspace’s own native review. The original Runtime transfer and installation controls carry the actual installation. The existing encrypted Collections recovery also carries the authoring records, completed request captures, native operator roots and original configuration filenames, including a period prepared before a purchase began.

**Return the whole editable operating record.** Associate an actual purchase only through its original buyer deployment, intent, transaction and useful-output evidence. The calendar stages the selected plan and associations into the existing Cohort review; planned entries begin with unverified transfer and unknown accepted-output status. The operator reviews the original evidence before any result can qualify. Reopening a saved Installation displays its original context and report; later missing, changed or voided source and purchase records appear separately. JSON, CSV and iCalendar exports retain the selected edition. Complete case export and independent receiving preserve the plan, source selection, all Installation editions and original business records so another operator can save the next edition.

**Completed Calendar operation.** The October 12 native run `customer-use-calendar-26b1-20261012` received the original operating-case archive at its actual version 37, retained its eight existing recorded testnet purchases and associated two records with their original selected buyers. It saved a twenty-entry plan, then a second edition with nineteen active entries after one cancellation; it also prepared the thirty-request and two-prepaid-group comparisons. The original Cohort seed kept transfer verification false and accepted output unknown. Native CLI and authenticated HTTP exports completed, and independent case receiving preserved both editions before saving and reopening edition three. The run created zero purchases and made zero provider requests. These eight retained case records remain a separate evidence scope from the application's eighteen team-operated development purchases. The [merged source and operating guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/c912e6ecb56a1f049901401d71f98be6cfd5dbb1/stellar/scf_2026/sf47_budget_model/workspace/CUSTOMER_USE_CALENDAR.md) retain the complete procedure; the private receiving package retains the original record identities and source bytes.

**Commission and accept a useful independent service.** The commissioning payer selects the useful resource, its source rights, the required output and the customer application that will receive it. The workorder identifies the merchant, independent buyer operator, maintainer and host/service-cost owner; it records the period or population, units, schema, complete output, price and selected payment terms. The reviewed product plan turns that requirement into a concrete installation and native receiving task. Acceptance follows one approved request through its actual transfer to the complete usable output, then has the receiving engineer reopen the same state and continue a later useful period. A payer can commission the installation and maintainable handover while an independent buyer separately purchases the resource. Later hosting, support and upgrades use the named operating responsibilities and separately agreed scope.

**Apply the foundation within the existing six packages.** These maintained workflows are the pre-award starting product. T1 resource integration adapts the selected source and customer output to the agreed service; T1 authority and handover connects its actual roles and a second accountable operator. T2 provider/ledger deployment and threat response implement the selected independent facilitators, monitoring and recovery behavior. T3 mainnet rollout and production recovery carry the deployed service into recurring independent use, receiving-host restore and support. Each remaining change is assigned once to its original package or a separately commissioned workorder. The grant retains $38,000, 400 prospective hours, 150 days and its original independent-use acceptance targets.

## Geospatial commissioning: a useful parcel decision and a complete receiving application

**The customer task.** Urban3's [published Pittsburgh case](https://www.urbanthree.com/case-study/pittsburgh-pa/) describes the difficulty of establishing which public entities own which parcels and resolving conflicts across municipal datasets. Its [Public Asset Valuation service](https://www.urbanthree.com/services/public-asset-valuation/) uses a portfolio view to support development scenarios and public-asset decisions. Our proposed contribution is the reproducible data preparation and analyst handover that supports that work: retain the original sources, reconcile parcel identities and owner assertions, record the responsible entity explicitly, and deliver a reviewed portfolio and native map. Urban3 would retain its valuation methods, scenarios, professional conclusions and client decisions.

**Worked source and current delivery.** The original Pittsburgh preparation contains 32 exact parcel keys, 29 City eProperty records, nine City tax-register records, 30 County assessment records and 29 parcel geometries. The native importer joined all 97 source records and preserved the unmatched keys. Each source file remains unchanged and carries its publisher and capture identity. The County response keeps its 87 original fields; the geometry source keeps the publisher's owner and tax-agent fields and its explicit EPSG:4326 response. The full 12,587-key City selection is a separate ongoing acquisition using those same source families. The complete [22-file parcel contribution](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/public-commons-sprint-2026/pull/2416), operating guide, native receiving programme and browser programme are merged. The [delivered complete product](https://chatgpt.com/api/library/files/libfile_c9c2ca1d5cb08191b76d9630faaff2b3/download) includes the editable software, installable QGIS plugin and nine original input files. Independent source review and native intake preparation are complete; the original full operator/browser/native-map programme is the next receiving result for this case.

**Operate the whole task.** Staff select the received source edition, inspect coverage and competing assertions, and review a parcel's original provider record beside its current decision. They can save a named accountable entity and retain its earlier versions, prepare a complete decision batch, review its exact preview, and save the selected decisions. A portfolio records the selected keys, assessment basis, area basis and grouping. Its complete JSON, parcel CSV and summary CSV retain the original tax year and as-of date; missing values remain explicit. Later source editions show added, removed, changed and unchanged parcel facts. Staff can carry unchanged reviews while retaining earlier frozen portfolios. The reviewed geometry and portfolio feed the existing native QGIS layer and project workflow. Full receiving carries source files, decisions, entity versions, portfolios, map resources, software and operating history so the next engineer can continue the same case.

**Agree the commercial and payment unit.** The [original proposed Urban3 workshare](https://chatgpt.com/api/library/files/libfile_96b917b3d6e8819186ed0e64dbd7e27b/download) is USD 7,200 over twelve active business days after written scope agreement, kickoff and the selected inputs. It covers one jurisdiction, up to 15,000 keys, four source families, an initial edition and one refresh, one correction and a 90-minute handover. This is the proposed implementation scope in the original company case. The selected grant installation separately names the commissioning payer, accountable merchant, independent buyer and receiving engineer. It defines a useful purchased unit, such as a reviewed dataset/asset selection or one complete commissioned report/project release. Public source access and professional valuation remain governed by their original terms; the selected merchant price applies to the agreed service and delivery.

**Connect that unit to Stellar.** For imagery and source datasets, the existing STAC merchant and native Dataset/Object buyers carry the reviewed request, immutable source edition, selected asset files and total cap through the original payment and complete receiving. For an agreed complete project file, the [original approved-order and paid-file workflow](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/public-commons-sprint-2026/blob/cc40a8fe0ca5f9f23956746ed730f8a0a4554a06/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf101-merchant-receiver/CHECKOUT.md) binds the actual file to its order, original settlement event and entitlement. The receiving engineer verifies the same delivered archive before importing it through the QGIS receiver. The customer gets its actual analysis input or maintained project; the merchant retains its original payment, fulfillment and support records. A later agreed source edition or a distinct customer analysis supplies repeat use with its own reviewed request.

**Apply the existing six funded packages.** T1 merchant-resource integration maps the selected customer's source/runtime, useful priced unit and typed receiving application; T1 authority and handover handles its actual source/terms changes and independent engineer access. T2 provider and ledger deployment runs the same useful service through both independently operated facilitators; T2 deployed threat response handles an interrupted settled purchase and a delivery failure with the original financial and file state. T3 mainnet rollout deploys the selected service and recurring consumer; T3 production recovery and handover carries the complete installation, restoration and maintained customer result. These are customer-specific Stellar adaptations of the delivered foundation within the existing USD 38,000, 400-hour and 150-day plan. The application's original independent-operator, purchase-window and returning-use definitions determine the funded cohort measurements.

Original source and proposed commissioning case · Complete product handoff · Same native receiving operation

## Institutional repository services and complete scholarly receiving

A university repository or implementation partner needs a collection that remains usable after migration: ordered contributors and affiliations, existing identifiers, distinct articles and complete issues, original access decisions and a working receiving application. The maintained TIND product provides that installation foundation. A commissioning workorder selects the actual collection, destination, acceptance task, implementation fee, included corrections and ongoing care.

### Installed source and customer workflow

The [complete installed operating guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/f0d521e2fb0f0cbed8912227a838041f2c5a4932/products/tind/OPERATING.md) and [original OAI intake application](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/f0d521e2fb0f0cbed8912227a838041f2c5a4932/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/oai-pmh/README.md) open the same repository workspace. Staff receive original HTTP responses or preserved original response bodies, review source coverage, select an edition, build its dataset and continue into editable TIND records. Original XML, acquisition history and staff decisions remain available throughout.

The retained Scholars Junction input contains 16 original responses. It includes a complete 15-record Endeavors journal edition and a separate staff collection of 11 individually returned GetRecord records. The latter carries four thesis access cases and seven journal cases: distinct licences, a complete issue, external full text, item-specific rights and an adviser, a named ORCID, and eleven ordered author affiliations. The complete original case and receiving programme retains the source bodies, exact populations and both operator modes.

The source's [Identify response](https://scholarsjunction.msstate.edu/do/oai/?verb=Identify) permits metadata reuse and requires prior written approval for robotic full-content harvesting. The application keeps metadata visibility, file access, dated release rules, licences and the original file or external-link relationship as separate decisions. Source refreshes reconcile the last delivered source, current source and current native destination; unrelated staff edits survive, and conflicting field groups receive an explicit staff choice.

The operator selects the actual institution, receives its native export, reconciles DOI/OAI identities and prepares a frozen batch. Actual native record and file results retain their original returned text, time, identifiers, byte identity and access observations. The complete handover reopens the editable repository, original sources, decisions, batches and later receiving history on another host. The original MSU programme carries its native execution and receiving result in that same case.

### Recurring service and Stellar use

The customer buys a working source-to-repository installation and separately scoped care. Recurring useful work can be a new journal edition, an agreed metadata query, a changed-access update or a comparison between source periods. The merchant publishes the exact priced HTTP or MCP resource; the buyer approves its complete result and aggregate cost, including required pages. The existing signing, facilitator, merchant and receiving components join that request to the observed Stellar transfer and usable customer output.

Publication cadence governs recurrence: a monthly issue produces a monthly edition, while a distinct requested query has its own accepted purpose. Original replay retains the same purchase and operation. The workorder records implementation, included support, service units, actual fees, collections and remaining effort. The cohort uses the application's existing definitions of independent buyers, useful purchases, complete tasks and original attempt windows.

### Remaining work in the funded programme

The completed source and migration product is the starting architecture. The [repository commissioning and grant guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/72619f000aa273e65d50d886625b15f284655912/products/tind/GRANT.md) assigns remaining customer work within the existing six packages. These are the shared programme allocations across both selected merchants.

|Existing funded package|Programme hours / cost|Repository-specific completion|
|  ---  |  ---  |  ---  |
|T1 merchant-resource integration|80 / $7,600|Operate the customer's agreed complete edition or query on its host and receive it in the buyer application.|
|T1 authority and handover|40 / $3,800|A second operator reopens the installation and completes the agreed source, access or withdrawal change.|
|T2 provider and ledger deployment|70 / $6,650|Complete the same useful metadata operation through both facilitators, joining approval, settlement and full output.|
|T2 deployed threat response|50 / $4,750|Operate monitoring and recovery for an interrupted paid delivery while preserving its financial result and unfinished work.|
|T3 mainnet rollout|90 / $8,550|Deploy the reviewed production service and recurring consumer configuration for independent useful customer use.|
|T3 production recovery and handover|70 / $6,650|Restore the repository and customer files on the receiving host, reconcile later work and complete a maintainer's support case.|


At customer selection and award acceptance, the original plan assigns each remaining adaptation once. It retains the $38,000, 400-hour, 150-day scope and existing two-merchant, two-buyer targets. Customer benefit compares the prior method, first installed task and later use on the same population: active effort, corrections, time to accepted output and unresolved work, with actual implementation, provider and support costs. The customer supplies any hourly-value assumption; original collections retain their actual cash basis.

## Retained services, facilitator choice and complete receiving

A merchant can change its payment provider while keeping the selected service, source edition and customer work together. The existing Socrata Publisher supplies that workflow in its browser, CLI and merchant MCP interface: choose the retained release and configured provider, inspect the complete native payment alternatives, retain the review and stage that reviewed release. The merchant then uses the existing activation, rollback and seller controls to select and run it.

### Work with the complete observed provider response

The [received-response implementation and operating guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/1b1c24ffb138ae6c1a60f5addd62e485ddddf37d/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf82-seller-pilot/FACILITATOR_RESPONSES.md) lets an available public source reader supply the whole provider response to the original operator. The portable document retains its endpoint, retrieval window, source attribution, content type and every original byte. The host profile selects the endpoint; the received document must match it.

The installed x402 SDK interprets those bytes and resolves the original service's complete ordered payment requirements. Its normalized value and the full original body remain separate, inspectable representations. This matters when a provider includes catalogue fields outside the SDK's supported-payment schema: an asset mentioned in a catalogue does not silently become an accepted payment alternative. The saved review binds the chosen host, original release digest, selection generation, normalized capabilities and exact native terms.

An operator can reopen a completed review and reconcile its already staged release after an interrupted reply. Changing the provider, source selection or captured document requires the matching review. The [Publisher guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/1b1c24ffb138ae6c1a60f5addd62e485ddddf37d/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/socrata/FACILITATORS.md) connects that retained work to release activation, seller startup, rollback and complete merchant-file receiving.

### The original Queens HPD operation

The original native case used the complete Vellar and Periplo responses captured on October 12, 2026: 857 and 394 bytes respectively. The installed x402 2.28.0 SDK completed both compatible reviews and staged both provider releases for the same retained Queens HPD service. The original service's source contains 1,342 historical project records; its acquired customer edition contains all 144 selected rows in the original two pages. Source creation time, both source captures and editions, the selected release and the complete customer CSV/JSONL remain in that original workspace.

The same original browser programme reopened both retained reviews and staged releases, downloaded the complete captured response, and completed its desktop and phone journey. The 390-pixel phone viewport remained 390 pixels wide. The source CLI then reopened and exported the original workspace, and an independent directory reopened the complete retained operator. These receiving steps preserve the original provider observations and customer edition.

Provider review and release staging have their own retained operation records. A qualifying paid customer use is measured from its original buyer request, observed settlement and complete useful output. The existing 144-row acquisition therefore keeps its two original purchases and one customer-task identity as this provider work proceeds.

### Customer installation within the funded programme

For a selected merchant, T1 commissions the real source, publishable scope, host profile and independent operator handover. T2's provider-and-ledger package applies this implemented workflow to the same useful customer service on both independently operated facilitators, then operates and reconciles the actual buyer purchases. T3 carries that selected production service, original results and unfinished work through the receiving engineer's restore and support operation.

The already completed reusable interfaces are the starting product. The existing six priced packages allocate the remaining customer-specific integration, deployment and maintainable handover. Customer acceptance includes the complete agreed edition or query, repeat useful use and another operator's ability to resume the original service.

## Connected Systems observations: customer commissioning and repeat use

A civil or environmental operator needs a defensible observation result that another analyst can use. The useful task begins with named systems and datastreams, a time window, the source's returned schema and a receiving application. It ends with the agreed population, original units and quality fields, a reviewed mapping, and a saved edition or query that the customer can reopen. A later observation period, source correction or distinct analytical request supplies repeat work.

GeoRobotix's [published engineering needs](https://georobotix.us/jobs/) include Connected Systems APIs and sensor-data integration. The original prepared workshare proposes one such customer installation for **$9,600, 72 engineering hours and 12 active business days**, with **$4,800 at commencement and $4,800 at accepted handover**. The message is prepared and unsent. GeoRobotix has not accepted the scope, nominated a customer, signed an agreement or paid for it.

### The customer operation and responsibilities

Under this proposal, the commissioning payer funds the integration. GeoRobotix retains its platform and customer relationship. The customer's technical owner supplies the approved endpoint, authentication reference, source rights and permitted retention, selected systems/datastreams and receiving environment. Its accepting operator agrees the useful queries and checks the delivered result. The implementation engineer configures and adapts the maintained product, corrects in-scope defects, packages it and completes handover. The proposal allows approximately three to five hours of customer participation for selection, review and receiving.

The operator starts with the actual returned JSON schema and raw response. Acquisition retains every acquired page, request and continuation, and records whether the selected window is exhausted, capped or failed. A configured bound does not establish complete history. Original numbers remain lexically intact; a numeric analytical projection is a reviewed mapping choice. The mapping carries source identifiers, timestamps, missing versus null values, units and quality fields into the edition.

The customer reviews that edition, runs the agreed query, and compares later editions using selected keys and duplicate handling. The package contains original source, mappings, configuration, saved results and the operating guide. A second engineer imports it into a separate workspace, reopens the result, reproduces the exact export and continues the same acquisition or review. External result links remain linked metadata; binary/video decoding and additional source families require separate scope.

### What has actually operated

The [complete product](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/pull/646) and its [selected installation guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/8883afe8b26545340db5d85e230cd1266af3c56e/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/selections/CONNECTED_SYSTEMS.md) are shipped. The original native operation completed schema and source review, an edition, query and export, independent import and exact re-export, and cold reopen. Its input is the publisher's [committed one-observation example](https://github.com/opengeospatial/ogcapi-connected-systems/blob/fb858be23aa03e2b824ec50b5a97ac2c2a1d3fec/api/part2/openapi/examples/observations/obs-simple.json), including the original 23.5 temperature value. It demonstrates the receiving workflow; it is not a live sensor collection or a customer deployment. Fifteen actual public endpoint error responses are retained separately.

The selected source archive has been built. Independent installation has reached dependency installation and is being continued from its original failure; installed receiving and browser acceptance are not yet established. No payment terms, live offer or merchant/buyer purchase is selected for this example. These limits define the remaining commissioning work without changing the completed native result.

### Twelve active business days to an accepted installation

The delivery starts after the parties agree access, selection, receiving environment and commencement payment. Provider or customer waiting time is recorded separately from active delivery days.

|Active days|Engineering hours|Complete output and acceptance|
|  ---  |  ---  |  ---  |
|1|6|Agree the actual response/schema, permitted selection and retention, receiving environment and useful acceptance queries.|
|2–4|18|Operate paged acquisition with original responses, explicit bounds, continuation, restart and provider-error handling.|
|5–6|12|Review field, time, unit and quality meanings; approve the mapping and first complete selected edition.|
|7|6|Run the agreed useful queries and compare editions while retaining their original source meanings.|
|8–9|12|Complete the customer's operator flow for selection, acquisition, mapping, editions, queries and recovery.|
|10|6|Install on the receiving host; import and reopen the same source, configuration and results.|
|11|6|Close the consolidated in-scope review; finalize source, notices, configuration and operator handover.|
|12|6|Complete the walkthrough and acceptance: the customer queries, compares and continues the retained operation.|
|**Total**|**72**|**One agreed JSON observation source and a complete receiving application.**|


Acceptance checks the declared window, received counts, duplicates and quality observations against the agreed source population. The operator must distinguish exhausted coverage from a capped or failed collection and must be able to reopen the original mapping and continue the retained operation. One consolidated review and in-scope defect correction are included. Additional endpoint families, changed outputs or wider integration receive a written scope, price and schedule before work begins. Hosting and provider charges are borne by the agreed party separately.

### Revenue, capacity and the existing award

The fixed fee pays for a defined installation and handover. It does not imply a platform subscription, a purchased dataset, payment principal or collected revenue. The fixed fee implies $133.33 per planned delivery hour. At the application's common **$95/hour planning rate**, 72 hours represent **$6,840** of effort and leave **$2,760** before other costs. A 25% effort overrun raises the modeled effort to 90 hours / $8,550 and leaves $1,050. These are planning comparisons, not actual payroll costs or a profit forecast. Actual effort, corrections, customer participation, invoices and collections remain in the original workorder and forecast.

Twelve active days average six engineering hours a day. The resulting 30-hour five-day workload cannot also occupy the same contributor's grant allocation. Bryce must assign actual available contributors and dates once across the commercial and funded work. The two proposed payments remain uncollected scenario cash until actual receipts exist.

If this candidate is selected as one of the two independent services, T1 completes its remaining merchant resource, buyer receiving and source-change authority; T2 deploys the same useful service through both independent facilitators and operates settlement/delivery recovery; T3 completes mainnet configuration, returning buyer work and receiving-host recovery. These changes remain within the existing six funded packages. Already completed engineering and separately paid customer work are excluded from the grant estimate or reconciled once before commitment, consistent with the [future-development funding rules](https://stellar.gitbook.io/scf-handbook/scf-awards/build-award/budget-and-deliverable-guidelines).

The merchant and buyer must agree the actual paid unit: a complete selected edition, a distinct saved query or another explicit resource. Paid pages, where applicable, retain their original prices and complete-task cost. A later useful observation period or query can count toward the existing cohort only after the original approval, observed native transfer and complete accepted result. The illustrative native example, a source archive, an installation retry and a prepared proposal add no qualifying purchase.

## Company research, recurring reference data and complete receiving

The installed company-research application turns an agreed legal-name or LEI population into reviewed company records, complete customer reports and a reusable native dataset. A researcher or software implementer can review inclusion, explain a changed company record and deliver a project that the receiving team can continue. GLEIF supplies free LEI access and CC0 data; the proposed service supplies TJLabs' research, source integration, operated refresh and receiving support. [Official API](https://www.gleif.org/en/lei-data/gleif-api/) · [Source data terms](https://www.gleif.org/en/meta/lei-data-terms-of-use).

### Complete useful customer operation

Open **Applications → GLEIF company research** or **starforge gleif**, select the customer's private project and agreed query, and capture every returned page or import complete original response envelopes. Retain the query, acquisition receipt and actual observation time. Review each company's legal name, LEI, separate entity and registration status, jurisdiction, addresses and original relationship references; save its inclusion decision, rationale, customer use and next work. Later refreshes become separate source editions. Compare their full records and explicitly resolve changed source or concurrent reviews.

Prepare the selected research as readable HTML, full JSON, machine CSV, spreadsheet CSV and JSONL. Each report retains the precise source and review editions selected for that delivery. The same company population becomes a native SF30 dataset with its declared filters and pagination. Export the whole project, receive it into a second private directory, open a company and its source, query the retained dataset and save the next agreed review. Browser, CLI, typed Node client and nineteen merchant tools share this operating state. [Complete operating guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/6ccf9f01147418338a0fee51b38b160fdcbacc5f/products/gleif/OPERATING.md) · [Original source and receiving contract](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/6ccf9f01147418338a0fee51b38b160fdcbacc5f/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/gleif/SOURCE_CONTRACT.md).

### Operated example and recurring customer value

The October 12 Foundation/Singapore-branch operation completed on Node 24.19.0 and Chromium 155. It covered original source downloads, retained stale drafts and explicit correction, both-company review, source comparison, all five customer formats, native dataset queries and independent project receiving with phone reopening. The final original project contains three source editions, eight review revisions, four reports and two native datasets; its initial browser operation and presentation continuation retained twenty-five desktop/phone views. The Singapore branch's Switzerland legal jurisdiction remains distinct from its Singapore legal address. Original source observation and project-save times remain separate.

A commercial workorder selects one company population and review period, a reviewer and receiving route, and the full report/dataset/project delivery. Subsequent periods provide fresh source editions, reviewed changes and the next usable customer package. Measure the customer's preceding and installed methods against that same population and completion criterion, recording actual source, review, correction and receiving effort. The [company-research commissioning guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/e68e824f7456cd21d91504b6407e48b8d650bf26/products/gleif/GRANT.md) supplies the complete operation and acceptance procedure. Original completed project and current native delivery.

### Selected Stellar deployment within the six funded packages

For a selected independent merchant, T1 joins the customer's dataset and receiving application to the actual service and completes source/terms authority and operator handover. T2 configures its native service through the two independent facilitators, carries the buyer's exact approval and transfer through complete company-data delivery, and operates interruption and recovery. T3 deploys the customer's mainnet host/network/asset configuration and recurring consumer, then completes off-host restoration, later-operation reconciliation and maintainer receiving. The finished research application supplies the starting product; remaining work is assigned to the original six packages. The programme retains its **$38,000 / 400 prospective hours / 150 days**, two-merchant and independent-buyer purchase targets.

Use the maintained runtime installation with native Stellar packages, the MCP feature and operator support. Retain the selected source archive, complete lock and READY installation. In Applications choose **Grant purchase reviewer**, select that runtime and a private workbench directory, then use **Review → Save → Connect → Start → Open**. Leaving Packet and SHA-256 empty selects the bundled original purchase; an existing exported packet uses its exact digest. The installed command is:

~~~sh
starforge grant-demo workbench --dir /srv/starforge/state/grant-review --port 0
~~~
